latestRelease.title: v1.18.19
latestRelease.notes:
## Core

### Improvements

- Added native OpenAI and Anthropic passthroughs for Cloudflare AI Gateway models.
- Matched Codex rate limits more closely to ChatGPT subscription limits. (@GameOn223)

### Bugfixes

- Removed built-in Qwen sampling defaults that could send unsupported settings.
- Properly show authenticated providers in `/connect`. (@OpeOginni)
- Ignore malformed model pricing instead of breaking usage cost calculation.
- Fall back when OpenAI websocket requests exceed message size limits.
- Forward ChatGPT workspace compute residency to Codex requests.
- Updated the default Console URL used by account connection flows.
- Enabled web search when using the OpenCode Go provider.
- Preserved compatibility with existing v1 databases.

## Desktop

### Bugfixes

- Kept saved server details editable in the server dialog.

**Thank you to 4 community contributors:**
- @TechyAditya:
  - fix(skills): Update global config path in documentation (#42337)
- @GameOn223:
  - tweak: match codex limits for openai models exactly when using chatgpt subscription (#39082)
- @OpeOginni:
  - fix(opencode): properly show authed providers on /connect command (#39915)
- @bhuvan2134686:
  - docs: add SCX.ai to the providers list (#42520)
highlights: Added native OpenAI and Anthropic passthroughs for Cloudflare AI Gateway models.
Matched Codex rate limits more closely to ChatGPT subscription limits. (@GameOn223)
Removed built-in Qwen sampling defaults that could send unsupported settings.

signals.title: TUI /sessions only show sessions from last 30 days, while CLI session list shows all my sessions (thank god)
signals.text: ### Description ### What breaks: The TUI `/sessions` picker only shows recent sessions and makes it look like older sessions are gone. ### What still works: `opencode session list` shows the full session history, and the CLI docs say session list should "List all OpenCode sessions." ### Why this is concerning The mismatch between TUI and CLI creates a false data-loss scare and blocks work. ### Expected behavior: - TUI `/sessions` should show the same session history that the CLI can list. - My entire session to stay unless I decide to prune them ### Actual behavior: TUI only shows recent sessions, while CLI can still see the old sessions ### Official docs reference: `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE` is documented as Disable pruning of old data, so users may assume old sessions are protected; the UI should not suggest they vanished when they still exist. ### Related issue: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13877: the existing report says the /sessions picker "only shows a small set of recent sessions." ### Help me confirm the accuracy of this: - Setting `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE=true` for future protection of my sessions, because that is the only official deletion-related control I could verify - Keep using `opencode session list` plus opencode session resume `<session_id>` until the TUI bug is fixed, because the CLI docs explicitly support listing all sessions and resuming by session ID. ### Related issues - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/16718 - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13877 ### Plugins @ramarivera/opencode-model-announcer ### OpenCode version 1.2.22 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Update to 1.2.22 2. Open TUI (`opencode`) 3. Write `/sessions` 4. Scroll all the way down only to see that sessions over 30 days are hidden 5. Exit TUI 6. Run `opencode list sessions` and thank the gods that older sessions are still listed there ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.title: bug: mouse escape sequences garbled after TUI exit
signals.text: ## Description After exiting the opencode TUI (via quit, Ctrl+C, or process stop), mouse escape sequences appear as garbled text in the terminal: ``` 35;89;19M35;84;20M35;76;22M35;71;23M35;67;23M35;67;24M35;67;25M35... ``` This is a separate issue from in-session mouse garbling (#3199 / PR #19520). The in-session bug is about fragmented SGR sequences leaking through StdinParser timeouts during active use. This bug occurs **after** the TUI has exited. ## Root Cause This is an upstream bug in `@opentui/core`'s `cleanupBeforeDestroy()` method. During renderer destruction, `stdin.setRawMode(false)` is called (re-enabling terminal ECHO) **before** mouse tracking is disabled. Any mouse events arriving during this window get echoed as raw escape sequence bytes. The correct ordering already exists in `@opentui/core`'s `suspend()` method, which calls `disableMouse()` before `setRawMode(false)`. **Upstream issue:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/904 **Upstream fix PR:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/905 ## Reproduction 1. Run `opencode` 2. Move the mouse while the TUI is active 3. Exit the TUI (quit or Ctrl+C) 4. Move the mouse in the shell immediately after exit 5. Garbled escape sequences appear ## Workaround A `patchedDependencies` patch for `@opentui/core` can fix this by adding `disableMouse()` + stdin drain before `setRawMode(false)` in `cleanupBeforeDestroy()`. A PR with this patch is forthcoming. ## Environment - macOS / Linux - Affects `@opentui/core@0.1.90` and `@opentui/core@0.1.95`

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Move git/PR instructions out of bash tool description to save ~1.7K tokens per request
signals.text: ﻿## Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ## Describe the enhancement you want to request I was profiling why a fresh OpenCode session starts at ~40K tokens. I downloaded all 16 tool .txt files from `packages/opencode/src/tool/` and measured them. **bash.txt is 9,288 characters (~2,654 tokens). But 63% of it has nothing to do with running bash commands.** The git commit workflow and PR creation instructions account for 5,874 characters (~1,678 tokens) — those are procedural guides, not bash execution semantics. Here's the thing: tool descriptions are sent with every single API request and are **not cacheable**. System prompt text, on the other hand, **is** cacheable (Anthropic prompt caching, OpenAI cached prefix). So those git/PR instructions are being paid for on every turn, even when the user never asks for a commit or PR. The fix is straightforward: move the `# Committing changes with git` and `# Creating pull requests` sections from `bash.txt` into the system prompt template. The model still sees the same instructions — just through a cacheable channel instead of a non-cacheable one. For reference, here's the full breakdown I measured: - bash.txt: 9,288 chars (~2,654 tokens) — 63% git/PR instructions - task.txt: 3,799 chars (~1,085 tokens) - multiedit.txt: 2,406 chars (~687 tokens) - edit.txt: 1,369 chars (~391 tokens) - apply_patch.txt: 1,092 chars (~312 tokens) - read.txt: 1,158 chars (~331 tokens) - lsp.txt: 1,040 chars (~297 tokens) - websearch.txt: 976 chars (~279 tokens) - batch.txt: 998 chars (~285 tokens) - codesearch.txt: 802 chars (~229 tokens) - webfetch.txt: 750 chars (~214 tokens) - question.txt: 657 chars (~188 tokens) - grep.txt: 689 chars (~197 tokens) - write.txt: 623 chars (~178 tokens) - glob.txt: 545 chars (~156 tokens) - ls.txt: 314 chars (~90 tokens) Total: ~26,500 chars (~7,573 tokens) across all built-in tool descriptions. This is complementary to the MCP lazy loading work in #12520 — that PR addresses dynamic MCP tools, while this addresses the static built-in tool overhead. Related: #11995, #17482, #20922.

signals.title: opencode (default mode) closes entire terminal window on Linux / i3wm
signals.text: ### Description ## Summary Running the `opencode` command in its default mode (which starts both the server and the TUI in the same process) causes the **entire terminal window to close** — not just the opencode process exiting, but the emulator window itself disappearing. Running `opencode serve` and `opencode attach <url>` as two separate processes works perfectly, which strongly suggests the bug is in the combined server+TUI startup path. ## Environment - **opencode version:** 1.14.21 - **OS:** Ubuntu (Linux) - **Window manager:** i3wm - **Shell:** zsh with oh-my-zsh - **Terminal emulators tested (all reproduce the bug):** xterm, Terminator, GNOME Terminal - **Installation path:** `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` - **Installation method:** curl installer (`curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`) — inferred from binary location at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open any terminal emulator (xterm, Terminator, GNOME Terminal — all reproduce). 2. Run `opencode` (default mode, no subcommand). 3. The TUI briefly appears, then the **entire terminal window closes**. ## Expected behavior The TUI should start and remain running until the user exits it. The terminal emulator window itself should never be closed by opencode. ## Actual behavior The terminal emulator window disappears entirely. The shell process and the emulator process both terminate. On the next session, running opencode reproduces the same crash. ## What works (workaround) Splitting the server and TUI into two separate processes works reliably: ```bash # Terminal 1 opencode serve --port 4096 # prints: http://127.0.0.1:4096 # Terminal 2 opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:4096 ``` In this mode, the TUI runs normally and the terminal does not close. This strongly suggests the bug is in the code path that launches server + TUI in a single process. ## Diagnostic work already done I ran an extensive elimination pass. The following were all tested and **ruled out** as causes: | Hypothesis | Test | Result | |---|---|---| | Out-of-memory (OOM killer) | `free -h`, `dmesg \| grep -i oom` | 20 GB RAM free, no OOM records | | Terminal emulator bug (VTE) | Tested in xterm (non-VTE) | Crash reproduces | | GPU/renderer issue | Multiple emulators tested | Crash reproduces in all | | Wrong binary architecture | `file $(which opencode)` + `uname -m` | Correct architecture | | Corrupted SQLite database | Moved `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db*` aside | No change | | Corrupted config/cache | Moved `~/.config/opencode/`, `~/.local/share/opencode/`, `~/.cache/opencode/` aside | No change | | Shell environment (zsh, oh-my-zsh, fnm, nvm) | `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin TERM=xterm /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c '~/.opencode/bin/opencode'` | Crash reproduces | | External plugins | `opencode --pure` | Crash reproduces | | Server alone | `opencode serve` | **Works fine** | | TUI alone attaching to external server | `opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:PORT` | **Works fine** | ## Strace findings Running `strace -f -o /tmp/opencode-strace.log opencode` and grepping for fatal signals showed **no SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, SIGKILL, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP** delivered to the main opencode process. Child processes exit cleanly with `exit_group(0)` (one exited with `exit_group(1)`, a grep subprocess whose command resolution I couldn't reconstruct from the log alone). The process disappears without any visible crash signature. The strace does show child processes resetting job-control signal handlers (`SIGTSTP`, `SIGTTIN`, `SIGTTOU` set to `SIG_DFL`) and redirecting stdin via `dup2(3, 0)` — consistent with opencode spawning shell subprocesses for tool calls during startup. My guess at the mechanism (not confirmed): the process that starts both server and TUI may be reparenting or detaching in a way that causes the controlling-TTY session leader to die, which then propagates up to the emulator. But this is speculation — someone familiar with the opentui integration would be far better placed to diagnose the real cause. ## Additional notes - **"Reinstalling" appeared to fix it temporarily** in earlier sessions. After full diagnosis, this was likely coincidental timing rather than a real fix — the crash reproduces consistently from a clean state. - The attach-based workaround is stable and usable indefinitely, so this is not blocking me personally, but the default `opencode` command being unusable on a common Linux configuration (Ubuntu + i3wm) seems worth fixing. ### Plugins linear (disabled) ### OpenCode version 1.14.21 ### Steps to reproduce I installed in the morning, and at night or in the next day the problem occurs when I open the opencode. The last times I just reinstalled, but this time I was able to build this workaround. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS ### Terminal xterm, Terminator, GNOME Terminal

signals.title: [Bug]: XDG Base Directory Spec violation — node_modules installed in ~/.config instead of ~/.local/share
signals.text: ### Description When running `opencode`, the application installs runtime dependencies (`node_modules`, `package.json`, and `package-lock.json`) into `~/.config/opencode`. This is a violation of the [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html). The `~/.config` directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) is strictly reserved for user-specific configuration files. Runtime data, dependencies, and state files should be stored in `~/.local/share` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME`). ### Why this is a problem - Many users back up their `~/.config` directory using tools like `git` (dotfiles), `stow`, or `chezmoi`. Placing `node_modules` in this directory causes massive repository bloat, sync issues, and forces users to manually add workarounds to their `.gitignore` files. - **Broken File Watchers:** Applications, background daemons, or text editors that monitor `~/.config` for configuration changes get overwhelmed or stuck in infinite reload loops due to the massive number of files and rapid I/O operations within `node_modules`. - **Loss of Configuration Portability:** Mixing mutable runtime dependencies with immutable configuration files breaks portability across different environments (Linux, macOS). It prevents users from symlinking their configs using tools like `stow`, as the application attempts to write heavy runtime data directly into the clean config structure. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.15.0 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Launch `opencode`. 2. Check the contents of the config directory: `ls ~/.config/opencode`. 3. Notice that `node_modules`, `package.json`, and `package-lock.json` are created there. ### Expected behavior - Configuration files stay in `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`). - Runtime dependencies, packages, and downloaded data should be placed in `~/.local/share/opencode/` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/`). ### Actual behavior Runtime dependencies and package tracking files are placed in `~/.config/opencode/`. ### Operating System Arch Linux ### Terminal Ghostty

signals.title: [Bug] OpenCode leaks temporary .so files in /tmp, consuming hundreds of GB over time
signals.text: ### Description ## Title: [Bug] OpenCode leaks temporary .so files in /tmp, consuming hundreds of GB over time ### Environment - OS: CentOS 7 / Linux x86_64 - OpenCode: latest (running May 2026) - Shell: bash ### Summary OpenCode generates temporary ELF shared object (`.so`) files in `/tmp` and **never cleans them up**. Over time, this accumulates into hundreds of gigabytes of disk space consumed by orphaned files. ### Reproducible Steps 1. Run OpenCode CLI for an extended period (days/weeks) 2. Observe `/tmp` directory ### Observed Behavior - OpenCode creates hidden `.so` files in `/tmp` with naming pattern: - `.5fff*-00000000.so` (4.3 MB each) - `.7bef*-00000000.so` (4.5 MB each) - `.fbff*-00000000.so` (4.5 MB each) - These are ELF 64-bit LSB shared objects (`file` output: "ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, not stripped") - New files are generated continuously (creation timestamps within seconds of current time) - **Old files are never deleted** — they accumulate indefinitely ### Impact On one system running OpenCode: | Metric | Before Cleanup | After Cleanup | |--------|---------------|---------------| | `/tmp` size | 728 GB | 252 MB | | `.so` file count | ~154,000 | 0 | | Disk usage | 1.8T / 1.9T (99%) | 1.1T / 1.9T (60%) | The system was running at 99% disk capacity, leaving only 30 GB free on a 1.9 TB disk. ### Root Cause Analysis Using `lsof`, confirmed that running `.opencode` processes hold these files as memory-mapped regions: ``` .opencode 15606 root mem REG ... /tmp/.7befcfab9d7f5ff9-00000000.so .opencode 27137 root mem REG ... /tmp/.7bef5fffbdff7fbf-00000000.so .opencode 72378 root mem REG ... /tmp/.5fffa7f6acff5fe7-00000000.so ... ``` This suggests OpenCode is generating JIT-compiled or dynamically-loaded shared libraries (possibly from V8 code caching or WASM compilation) but lacks any cleanup mechanism — no tmpwatch integration, no file rotation, no cleanup on process exit. ### Expected Behavior - Temporary files should be cleaned up when the process exits - Or at minimum, a bounded number of files should be retained (e.g., LRU eviction) - Or use a dedicated temp directory (e.g. `/tmp/opencode/`) that is cleaned on startup ### Workaround Added a cron job to clean old `.so` files daily: ``` 0 2 * * * find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name ".*.so" -type f -mtime +1 -delete ``` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Per-agent MCP tool filtering to stay within model tool limits
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. > **Related issues (not duplicates):** > - #17607 requests per-agent tool allow/deny with glob patterns — similar scope but focused on trust/role separation, not model tool limits. Our issue is complementary. > - #23297 requests a `hidden` field on `tool.definition` hook — overlaps with our Option B, but without `agent` context in the input it cannot solve per-agent filtering. We need both `hidden` + `agent` in the hook input. > - #7399 (closed) requested `includeTools`/`excludeTools` per MCP server config — global, not per-agent. --- ## Problem When using models with a hard tool limit (e.g. GPT-4o mini / `github-copilot/gpt-5-mini` with a 128-tool cap), agents that don't need all configured MCP servers still receive every tool definition in their context. This causes the request to exceed the model's tool limit and fail. **Example setup:** - 3 MCP servers configured globally: `gitlab` (~40 tools), `jira` (~30 tools), `sonarqube` (~20 tools) - `librarian` agent uses `gpt-5-mini` (128-tool limit) - `librarian` only needs built-in tools + web search — it has no use for gitlab/jira/sonarqube - Total tools sent to `librarian`: 90+ MCP tools + built-in tools → exceeds 128 ## What doesn't work today ### `permission: deny` (opencode native + oh-my-openagent) ```json { "agents": { "librarian": { "permission": { "gitlab_*": "deny", "jira_*": "deny" } } } } ``` Blocks *execution* of those tools but does **not** remove them from the tool list sent to the model. The model still sees all tool definitions and they still count toward the limit. ### `tools: { "gitlab_*": false }` (oh-my-openagent agent override) oh-my-openagent migrates this to `permission: deny` internally — same problem, same result. ### `tools: { "gitlab_*": false }` (opencode native agent config) The `tools` key is not a recognized opencode agent field. It is silently routed into `options` and has no effect whatsoever. ### `tool.definition` plugin hook Only receives `toolID` — no agent context. Cannot conditionally filter per agent. ## Requested feature One or more of the following: ### Option A: Per-agent `disabled_mcps` in opencode agent config ```json { "agent": { "librarian": { "disabled_mcps": ["gitlab", "jira", "sonarqube"] } } } ``` Mirrors the top-level `disabled_mcps` that oh-my-openagent already supports, but scoped to a single agent. ### Option B: Agent context + `hidden` field in the `tool.definition` plugin hook ```ts "tool.definition"?: (input: { toolID: string; agent: string; // add this — needed for per-agent filtering }, output: { description: string; parameters: any; hidden?: boolean; // add this (as also requested in #23297) — removes tool from LLM tool list }) => Promise<void>; ``` Would allow plugins to filter tools per agent without needing native config support. Note: `hidden` alone (#23297) is insufficient — the `agent` field in the input is also required. ### Option C: Native `tools` filter in opencode agent config ```json { "agent": { "librarian": { "tools": { "gitlab_*": false, "jira_*": false } } } } ``` A glob-based allowlist/denylist that removes matching tools from the tool list before it is sent to the model. ## Why this matters - Models with small tool limits (GPT-4o mini, o1-mini, etc.) are unusable as sub-agents when many MCP servers are configured globally - Specialized agents (librarian, explore, reviewer) have well-defined tool needs — giving them 100+ irrelevant tools wastes context tokens and hits limits - The current workaround (disabling MCPs globally) defeats the purpose of having them configured ## Environment - opencode (latest) - oh-my-openagent plugin - MCP servers: gitlab, jira, sonarqube - Affected agent: `librarian` (model: `github-copilot/gpt-5-mini`, 128-tool limit)
signals.author: CrystalMethod

signals.title: [QUESTION]: Plugin notification API — signal context to user (status bar, toast, etc.)
signals.text: ## Use case Our plugin injects memory context into the system prompt via `experimental.chat.system.transform`. In Claude Code, the plugin could signal "3 memories loaded" in the status bar. In OpenCode, we have no way to surface this to the user short of injecting visible text into the system prompt itself. ## What we're looking for A lightweight notification mechanism that plugins can use to signal state to the user — e.g.: - Status bar message: "Memory: 3 contexts loaded for mcp-memory-service" - Toast/banner: "Session summary stored" - Some hook/API: `client.ui.notify({ level: "info", message: "..." })` ## What we tried - `client.app.log({ service, level, message })` — writes to internal log, invisible to user during session - Injecting `<memory-context>3 memories loaded</memory-context>` via `experimental.chat.system.transform` — works but clutters the system prompt ## Question Is a plugin user-notification API planned or already available via some hook we missed?
signals.author: doobidoo

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Incrementally update AGENTS.md to improve input cache hit rate
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Under the current implementation, when the content of `AGENTS.md` is modified during the lifecycle of a session, it will be reloaded into the system prompt segment at the very beginning of the context, causing all subsequent tokens to miss the cache. **Tested Environment:** OpenCode 1.15.10 with DeepSeek V4 Pro on Linux **Reference implementation:** Referring to Claude Code's behavior, the content of CLAUDE.md is loaded into the system prompt only when the session is created. If `CLAUDE.md` is later modified, Claude Code would insert a `<system-reminder>` to indicate that the content of `CLAUDE.md` has been changed, rather than directly modifying the system prompt.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Modify system prompt to improve cache hit rate
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request I previously submitted an issue mentioning the impact of AGENTS.md on cache hit rates. See: #29584 Additionally, I have found that the environment information and the skills list in the system prompt also affect the cache hit rate. Currently, the environment information in the system prompt includes: model id & provider, working directory, workspace root folder, git repo flag, platform, today's date. Below is my analysis of each field's impact on cache hits: - ✅ **model id & provider:** It only changes when switching models, and different models have different KV caches, so switching models naturally leads to cache misses. So this field is fine. - ✅ **working directory:** Once a session is created, this field does not change dynamically, and it is information the LLM needs to know. - ✅ **platform:** This field is stable, would not change during the lifetime of a session, and is also information the LLM needs to know. - ❌ **workspace root folder & git repo flag:** In my testing, in a non-git repo directory, workspace root folder is /, and git repo flag is false. While the session remains in the foreground and I run git init in that directory, neither field changes. However, once I exit opencode and resume the session after `git init` or `rm -r .git`, workspace root folder becomes the same as the working directory, and git repo flag becomes true, causing all subsequent token caches to miss. - ❌ **today's date:** After crossing midnight, this field changes, causing all subsequent token caches to miss. DeepSeek servers may keep caches on disk for several hours or even days; the cache miss caused by the date change is unnecessary. Therefore, I suggest the following regarding the env section of the system prompt: - Remove workspace root folder and git repo flag. The agent can use git commands to check whether the current path is a git repo. I don't think this information needs to be in the system prompt. - Remove today's date. The agent can also query this using commands. I don't think this information needs to be in the system prompt either. In addition to the modifications to the env section of the system prompt, I also suggest placing the skill list before env. Because the skill list is more stable than env (e.g., working directory), this will yield better cache hit rates when using opencode in different working paths. Related code `packages/opencode/src/session/system.ts:42-80` OpenCode version: 1.15.10

signals.title: High CPU usage in newer versions of OpenCode
signals.text: ### Description Since around 7 days ago, the CPU usage of OpenCode has spiked dramatically. Before, I was able to use over 10 OpenCode sessions at the same time; since the last updates, my PC has problems with 3. ~~The result of this is a heavily slowed-down and laggy mouse cursor reaction time; therefore, you can't properly use OpenCode nor anything else.~~ Unrelated to OpenCode; same behaviour on my end by using [CpuStress](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/cpustres) for finding this out. I can't say for sure when this error appeared; however, reverting to v1.14.51 fixed it. Also, I noticed that in Task Manager, as I launch it inside VSCode (X in standalone terminal, PowerShell in my case), at v1.15.12 - one of the problematic versions - it shows Bun (which OpenCode uses) as a stand-alone process there, but after I reverted to v1.14.51, it's back again included as a subprocess of VSCode. Both versions installed using npm X desktop app (at least its new versions) have the same behaviour. ### Plugins Used some plugins --> deactivated them --> no difference ### OpenCode version Problematic: v1.15.12 + few older ones (v1.15.X); without error: v1.14.51 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install a new version of OpenCode (like v1.15.12) - desktop or terminal 1B (opt.). Install VSCode 2. Launch multiple sessions of OpenCode. The more, the better. 3. In each session, provide it with a task (for example, some refactoring, researching, analysing, etc.; so it'd use the codebase you use). 4. See and check the CPU usage of Bun for each one. 5. Uninstall the new version, install the older one (like v1.14.51), and repeat steps 2-4. 6. Compare CPU usage between versions. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal PowerShell (standalone/in VSCode)

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Feature Request / Bug: Cannot set context window limits for local models via GUI/TUI (Defaults to 0)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Description When connecting OpenCode to a local OpenAI-compatible provider (e.g., Jan AI, LM Studio, Ollama) using custom models, OpenCode often fails to fetch the model's context window metadata from the local API. As a result, the context limit defaults to 0 in the TUI. This breaks context tracking and auto-compaction. Currently, the only way to fix this is by manually editing the opencode.json configuration file to include a limit block. Users should be able to define or override these limits directly within the GUI/TUI. Steps to Reproduce Run a local LLM via a provider like Jan AI (e.g., Qwopus3.6-27B-v2-Q8_0.gguf). Add the custom provider to opencode.json using the @ai-sdk/openai-compatible npm package. Open the OpenCode TUI and select the local model via the /models menu. Look at the session context tracker — it displays 0 for the context limit. Expected Behavior When OpenCode cannot automatically determine a model's context window, or when a user wants to artificially limit it, there should be an option within the TUI (perhaps in the /models menu or a dedicated settings menu) to manually input the Context Limit and Output Limit. Actual Behavior The context defaults to 0. The user is forced to leave the UI, locate their opencode.json file, and manually write a JSON block to define the limits: JSON "limit": { "context": 250000, "output": 8192 } Proposed Solution Add an "Edit Model Limits" or "Set Context Size" option directly in the GUI when selecting custom or local models. This UI prompt would accept context and output integers and automatically write them to the underlying config file, removing the need for manual JSON editing. Environment / Context Provider: Local OpenAI-compatible APIs (Jan AI) Model: Custom local .gguf files Impact: High friction for local/offline users who frequently switch between models with varying context sizes (e.g., 8k vs 250k).

signals.title: File Tree Cache Persists After Folder Deletion
signals.text: ### Description Application: opencode-desktop v1.17.3 (Electron 42.3.3) OS: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04) Issue: File tree component displays "Failed to list files" toasts for folders that no longer exist on disk. Description After creating and then deleting a folder (apps/asalkita2) within an opencode Desktop workspace, the file tree UI continues to show error toasts for subdirectories inside that deleted folder. The cache appears to be stored in a location that survives: Deleting the folder from disk Deleting the entire .config/ai.opencode.desktop/ directory Restarting the opencode desktop application process Rebooting the machine Steps to Reproduce Create a folder in the workspace: mkdir -p apps/test-Project/static/promotion-media1/{mobile,desktop} Open opencode Desktop and expand the folder in the file tree Close opencode Desktop Delete the folder: rm -rf apps/test-Project Reopen opencode Desktop Observe error toasts for apps/test-Project/static/promotion-media1/mobile and desktop Expected Behavior The file tree should reflect the current filesystem state. Deleted folders should not appear in the tree nor cause errors. Actual Behavior The file tree shows "Failed to list files" toasts for paths inside the deleted folder. The cache is read when the renderer requests directory listings, even though the paths don't exist. Investigation Notes The error comes from FileSystem.list() in the opencode server process The cache is not in: SQLite database (opencode.db), git snapshot, or Chromium Local Storage The opencode.global.dat only stores fileTree: {opened, width, tab} — NOT expanded directory state The cache appears to be embedded in the bundled app.asar or stored in an unidentified internal location Workaround (Temporary) Creating empty placeholder directories for the cached paths silences the errors: mkdir -p apps/fe/{tests,static/{samples,promotion-media1/{mobile,desktop}}} Additional Info This is not the first opencode Desktop issue we've encountered with persistent file tree state storage. Related debugging revealed that the file tree expanded/collapsed state does not appear to be persistently stored in any obvious location, yet the deleted folder's structure continues to be "seen" by the server. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Copilot Claude Opus 4.8 assistant prefill 400 after malformed pseudo tool-call text
signals.text: ## Description `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8` can reject a follow-up request with: ```text APIError 400: This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message. isRetryable: false ``` After re-checking local SQLite metadata on OpenCode 1.17.7, this now appears to be downstream of the malformed pseudo tool-call issue in #31247. The observed chain is: 1. Opus 4.8 emits pseudo tool-call text such as `<invoke ...>` as assistant text. 2. The assistant message is still marked `finish=tool-calls`. 3. There is no structured tool part in that assistant message. 4. OpenCode continues the tool loop. 5. The next provider request effectively ends with an assistant message. 6. Copilot Claude rejects that request as unsupported assistant prefill. ## Steps to Reproduce I do not yet have a small deterministic repro, but the failures occurred in normal OpenCode TUI sessions using `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8`: 1. Start an OpenCode TUI session with `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8`. 2. Perform a long tool-heavy task. 3. Continue through multiple automatic tool-call turns. 4. Hit a malformed Opus 4.8 turn where `finish=tool-calls`, there are zero structured tool parts, and the assistant text contains pseudo tool-call markup such as `<invoke ...>`. 5. Observe the next request fail with the assistant-prefill 400. ## Expected Behavior OpenCode should not send a Copilot Claude request whose final message is assistant. More importantly, OpenCode should handle a malformed `finish=tool-calls` response with no actual tool call at the root, instead of continuing the tool loop with an assistant-ending history. ## Actual Behavior The provider rejects the follow-up request with: ```text This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message. ``` Every sampled prefill 400 was immediately preceded by a `claude-opus-4.8` assistant message with this structure: ```text finish: tool-calls structured tool parts: 0 assistant text contains: <invoke ...> ``` Sampled chain: | Error message | Previous message | Previous finish | Previous tool parts | Previous text contains `<invoke>` | |---|---|---|---:|---:| | `msg_ea14109c...` | `msg_ea140d8ac...` | `tool-calls` | 0 | yes | | `msg_ea14ee3d...` | `msg_ea14ec5d...` | `tool-calls` | 0 | yes | | `msg_ea1565f9...` | `msg_ea1562db...` | `tool-calls` | 0 | yes | ## Additional Evidence Downstream symptom evidence: https://gist.github.com/doomsday616/659c12bc0d0f02dff5a605e2ea6ec4cd Root-cause evidence is in #31247: https://gist.github.com/doomsday616/d3fb56acd0f14964a9797df35f1fcd96 Both gists contain only sanitized structural metadata from local SQLite rows. Private message text and local/private identifiers are not included. ## OpenCode Version ```text 1.17.7 ``` ## Operating System ```text Windows 11 ``` ## Terminal ```text Windows Terminal / PowerShell 7 ``` ## Provider / Model ```text github-copilot / claude-opus-4.8 ``` ## Related Issues - #31247 — likely root cause: Opus 4.8 pseudo tool-call text persisted as assistant text while `finish=tool-calls` and no structured tool part exists. - #13768 — same/similar assistant-prefill rejection with GitHub Copilot + Claude Opus. - #19517 — Azure AI Claude via LiteLLM rejects assistant prefill. - #29760 — Bedrock Claude Opus 4.6 rejects assistant prefill. ## Sanitization The original full session contains private content, so I cannot share a raw export publicly. The linked evidence includes only sanitized structural excerpts and provider error metadata.

signals.title: [BUG] Subagent terminates prematurely mid-execution but reports completed
signals.text: ## Description Subagent terminates before completing its work, but the task tool reports it as "completed". The parent agent receives partial/incomplete output. The output size is well under the 50KB/2000-line truncation limit. ## Observed behavior 1. Primary agent calls `task(subagent_type="explore", prompt="...")` to explore a codebase 2. Subagent starts working (reading files, searching with glob/grep) 3. Subagent stops mid-way through exploration — only examined some of the requested files/directories 4. Task tool returns the partial result as "completed" 5. Parent agent receives incomplete information, unaware that the subagent didn't finish ## Key details - Output size is minimal (far below 50KB/2000-line limit) - No error is surfaced - Subagent status shows "completed" - Issue is NOT about text truncation (the output is fully delivered but incomplete) - Issue is about the subagent execution being cut short ## Related issues - #6792: Task Tool Timeouts & Early Termination (similar root cause — subagent termination) - #11903: Task tool truncation drops session_id metadata - #11865: Tasks/Subagents with Codex / OpenAI are frequently getting stuck - #24342: Main & Sub-agents Randomly Freeze Indefinitely ## Suspected causes 1. Hardcoded timeout in Task tool (~30-60s) killing the subagent session 2. LLM provider response timing out mid-conversation 3. Tool call (grep/glob/read) hanging and aborting the subagent loop ## Expected behavior - Subagent should complete all tool calls and analysis before returning - If terminated early, should report "error" or "timeout" instead of "completed" - Parent agent should be informed when subagent did not fully complete ## Environment - opencode version: latest - Platform: linux - Subagent type: explore
signals.author: YoungJurry

signals.title: Deepseek and MCPs ($ref/$defs in MCP tool schemas causes AttributeError)
signals.text: ### Description **Title**: DeepSeek provider: $ref/$defs in MCP tool schemas causes AttributeError **Description**: **Version**: opencode 1.17.5 **Provider**: DeepSeek Affected MCP servers: Asana (mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp), Notion (@notionhq/notion-mcp-server) **Error:** Error from provider: Error resolving schema reference '#/$defs/richTextRequest': AttributeError("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lookup'") **Possible cause**: MCP servers output valid JSON Schema 2020-12 with $ref → $defs references. DeepSeek's API (like Fireworks, Anthropic, Gemini) strictly validates schemas and rejects unresolved $ref pointers. The same error occurs with Notion MCP (#/properties/sections/items/properties/tasks/items/properties/assignee). **Expected fix**: opencode should dereference/flatten $ref before sending to DeepSeek — similar to the Gemini sanitization done in #12292. Workaround: Disable affected MCP servers or switch to a provider that handles $ref natively (e.g. OpenAI). **References**: - LiteLLM #26692 — identical error with Fireworks - opencode #12292 / #12295 — Gemini fix for same class of problem - FastMCP #2808 — schema dereferencing for MCP client compatibility ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.5 ### Steps to reproduce { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "small_model": "google/gemini-3-flash-preview", "mcp": { "asana": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "{env:ASANA_MCP_CLIENT_ID}", "clientSecret": "{env:ASANA_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET}" } }, "chrome-devtools": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest"] }, "figma": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "figma-mcp"] }, "notion-sys": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"], "environment": { "NOTION_TOKEN": "xyz" } }, "notion-lv": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"], "environment": { "NOTION_TOKEN": "xyz" } } } } ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System macOS 26.4.1 ### Terminal Nova, System bash

signals.title: Import sessions after runtime change to rust does not work
signals.text: ### Description Assume you have exported a session to json file, using version 1.15.4. When you trying to import this version in a new opencode, for example 1.17.8 it will fail and print unrelated message like "file not found" I ask opencode to try to research the issue and it found that previous version exported file in Utf16-LE format that newest version cannot read (only Utf-8 supported) Here is AI reply: `The session imported successfully after converting to UTF-8 without BOM. Root cause: The file ses_1bf8a86b1ffeNAd6lVyuCurdUt.json was exported by opencode 1.15.4 in UTF-16 LE encoding (with BOM). The opencode import command (1.17.8) uses a Rust binary that expects UTF-8 without BOM and fails with a misleading "File not found" error when it can't decode the file. Fix: Convert the file to UTF-8 (without BOM): $content = Get-Content -LiteralPath "ses_1bf8a86b1ffeNAd6lVyuCurdUt.json" -Raw [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText("ses_utf8.json", $content, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)) opencode import ses_utf8.json The session format itself (1.15.4) was compatible with 1.17.8 import — only the encoding was the issue.` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.8 ### Steps to reproduce 1. export any session using version 1.15.4 to a json file 2. try to import the session with the latest version ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows terminal
signals.author: kirillp

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Surface AXI CLI tools alongside MCP servers in TUI sidebar
signals.text: ### Verified - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request OpenCode's experimental resource endpoint already scans `~/.local/bin/*-axi` and serves AXI CLI tool information alongside MCP servers. Currently this data only appears in the MCP status popover but not in the TUI sidebar. **Request**: Wire AXI CLI tool data into the TUI sidebar so users can see which AXI tools are available (gh-axi, npm-axi, chrome-devtools-axi, cluster-ops-axi) alongside their MCP servers. **Proposed changes**: - TUI sidebar header changes from "MCP" to "MCP/AXI" when AXI tools are present - AXI tools render as read-only info items below MCP servers (no toggle switches — AXI tools are filesystem-based, not server processes) - Add `mcp_resource` accessor to TUI plugin adapter - Add `mcp_resource` to `TuiState` type definition **Why this belongs in OpenCode**: This completes the AXI tool visibility story — the backend already scans and serves this data, but the TUI (the primary interface) doesn't show it. Users who have AXI tools installed should see them in the sidebar to understand what tools are available to their agents.

signals.title: OpenAI Responses (gpt-5.5): 500 server_error doom-loop when too many tools are enabled
signals.text: ### Summary When many tools are enabled (e.g. several MCP servers), opencode sends every tool definition in a single OpenAI Responses request. The ChatGPT/Codex OAuth backend rejects requests carrying too many tools with a generic 500 `server_error`. Because the retry policy has no attempt cap for 5xx, opencode then retries the same oversized request indefinitely — turning it into a multi-hour doom-loop that makes the model (e.g. gpt-5.5) effectively unusable. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a setup with a large number of enabled tools (many MCP servers — ~870 tool definitions in my case). 2. Use an `@ai-sdk/openai` model on the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth path (e.g. gpt-5.5). 3. Send any prompt that triggers a model turn. ### Expected The request succeeds, or fails with an actionable error. ### Actual The backend returns a 500 `server_error` and opencode retries the identical request with no cap, looping for hours. ### Notes on root cause - Reproduced with 876 tool definitions: 5 `server_error`s and a stuck loop. The same prompt with `--pure` (11 tools) works, confirming tool **count** is the trigger — not schema, request size, or reasoning threading. - The retry policy applies to 5xx with no max-attempt cap, which amplifies the single rejection into the loop. ### Environment - Model: gpt-5.5 (OpenAI Responses, ChatGPT/Codex OAuth) - Runtime: AI-SDK path (`@ai-sdk/openai`)
signals.author: sjawhar

signals.title: [FEATURE]: MCP tool calls should carry current session context (session_id)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Feature Request When OpenCode calls an MCP tool, the current session ID should be injected into the request so that MCP servers can associate operations with the OpenCode session that triggered them. ### Use Case I built an MCP server (`mcp-memory`) that stores conversation memories. It accepts an optional `session_id` parameter, but when OpenCode's AI agent calls `save_memory`, it doesn't know the current session ID, so memories are saved without session context. This makes it impossible to group memories by the OpenCode session they originated from. ### Proposed Solution Inject the current OpenCode session ID into MCP tool call requests via the `_meta` field of the `CallToolRequest` (following MCP protocol design). This approach works for both local (stdio) and remote MCP servers, unlike solutions that only cover HTTP transport. The MCP server would then extract the session ID from the request context. ### Why this matters Without session context, memory/stateful MCP servers have no way to correlate data with the conversations that produced them, limiting their usefulness for cross-session persistence. ### Relationship to existing issues This request differs from related issues: - **#15117** proposes exposing session context via environment variables (`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`). While valuable, env vars are set at process start and cannot change mid-session. Our `_meta` field approach follows MCP protocol design and works per-request. - **#28225** proposes a plugin hook (`mcp.call.before`) to inject headers into outbound HTTP MCP calls. This only covers remote MCP over HTTP transport. Our `_meta` field approach covers both local (stdio) and remote MCP servers uniformly.
signals.author: liaosf

signals.title: Subagent sessions created with model=undefined causing ProviderModelNotFoundError
signals.text: ## Description All built-in subagent types (`general`, `explore`, `code-reviewer`, etc.) fail with `ProviderModelNotFoundError` when spawned via the `task` tool. The subagent session is created with `model=undefined` instead of inheriting the agent's configured model. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Use any built-in subagent type via the `task` tool: ``` task(description="test", subagent_type="general", prompt="read a file") ``` 2. Observe the error: `ProviderModelNotFoundError` 3. Check the opencode log at `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` ## Log Evidence ``` message=created id=ses_... agent=general model=undefined ... message="share subscriber failed" type=message.updated cause=Cause([Fail(ProviderModelNotFoundError)]) ``` The `model=undefined` is visible in every subagent session creation log entry. The agent config correctly shows the model (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), but it is not passed to the spawned subagent session. ## Agent Config (correct) ``` opencode debug agent general "native": true, "model": { "providerID": "deepseek", "modelID": "deepseek-v4-flash" ``` ## Environment - opencode version: 1.17.8 (also tested on 1.17.2 — same issue) - OS: macOS (darwin) - Provider: deepseek - Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash ## Workaround All work must be done inline in the main thread — subagents cannot be used.

signals.title: [BUG] Feishu plugin: orphaned sessions continue looping after abort, causing sustained high CPU
signals.text: ## Problem When a Feishu (飞书) session is **aborted** by the user (e.g., via cancel in the Feishu UI), the session is marked as `orphan=true` but its processing **loop is not terminated**. The opencode process continues to re-enter the loop (`step=0 → step=1 → ...`), making repeated LLM inference requests indefinitely. If the parent terminal/process exits, the opencode main process becomes an orphan (PPID=1) and **keeps consuming high CPU** (observed 370-420% CPU, ~8.5GB RSS) with no way to stop it except manually killing the process. ## Root Cause The Feishu plugin's `session.error` handler logs `orphan=true` but does **not** properly clean up the session's pending tasks or prevent the session from re-entering the processing loop. This is distinct from the existing orphan session issues (#19023, #30683, #31787) which deal with DB records or project ID drift — this is specifically about the **Feishu WebSocket channel** triggering repeated loop restarts for aborted sessions. Additionally, when the Feishu WebSocket connection drops (e.g., certificate verification errors), the reconnect logic may trigger re-processing of orphaned sessions. ## Reproduction 1. Start opencode with Feishu plugin configured 2. Send a message from Feishu to trigger a session 3. Cancel/abort the session from the Feishu UI 4. Observe that the session is marked `orphan=true` but continues looping 5. Close the terminal running opencode 6. The opencode process becomes orphaned (PPID=1) and continues consuming high CPU ## Observed Logs ``` level=ERROR message=process session.id=ses_xxx error=Aborted stack=undefined level=WARN message="[feishu] 收到 session.error 事件" sessionId=ses_xxx errMsg=Aborted orphan=true level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_xxx step=0 // <-- loop restarts despite orphan=true level=INFO message=stream providerID=omlx modelID=Qwen3___5-122B-A10B-4bit session.id=ses_xxx ``` ## Expected Behavior When a session is aborted and marked as orphan, the Feishu plugin should: 1. Remove the session from the active processing queue 2. Not allow the session to re-enter the loop on subsequent iterations 3. Clean up any pending message handlers for that session ## Environment - Opencode version: 1.17.8 - Platform: macOS ARM64 (Darwin) - Model: oMLX local (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-4bit) - Feishu plugin: WebSocket mode (persistent connection) ## Related Issues - #19023 — Sessions permanently stuck after server restart or stream interruption - #31787 — Effect.orDie orphans subagent sessions after tool error - #20099 — Runtime watchdog for stuck tool/session recovery - #22542 — Feishu media type error - #27642 — Feishu locale routing issue

signals.title: sampledChecksum() skips the last ~2KB of content, causing stale file caches
signals.text: ### Description `sampledChecksum()` in `packages/core/src/util/encode.ts` (line 42) uses `content.length - size` as the last sampling point. The window is centered on each point and clamped to `[0, content.length - size]`, so the last window covers `[content.length - 6144, content.length - 2048]` — the final ~2KB of the content is never hashed. This function is used as a cache key in `packages/ui/src/components/file.tsx` (line 1089) and `packages/app/src/pages/session/file-tabs.tsx` (line 202). Edits to the end of a large file (>500KB) produce the same cache key, so the UI shows stale content. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a file larger than 500KB in the TUI 2. Edit the last few lines of the file 3. The file viewer cache key does not change because the last 2KB is excluded from the sampled checksum 4. The UI continues showing the pre-edit content ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal N/A

signals.text: The observability setup currently always uses OTLP HTTP JSON for logs and traces, even when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf or signal-specific protocol env vars are configured. This breaks setups where the OTLP collector expects protobuf payloads. Expected behavior: - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf enables protobuf for logs and traces. - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_PROTOCOL and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL override the general protocol for their signal. - Unsupported protocol values fall back to JSON.

signals.title: Session list not displaying sessions after auto-compaction
signals.text: ## Bug Description After a long session triggers auto-compaction, the session disappears from the session list UI. The session still exists in the database (confirmed via `session_list` API), but the UI does not display it. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Have a long session (>1000 messages) that triggers auto-compaction 2. After compaction, the session is no longer visible in the session list UI 3. Workaround: Switching to another project and back temporarily makes it reappear 4. Creating a new session causes the old session to disappear from the list again 5. However, calling `session_list` API still returns the session with correct metadata ## Expected Behavior Compacted sessions should continue to appear in the session list UI alongside other sessions. ## Actual Behavior The session list UI does not show compacted sessions. The session data is intact (confirmed via API), suggesting a UI rendering/caching issue rather than data loss. ## Affected Session - Session ID: `ses_1220f1f20ffeGlybAZ8N8U3S0e` - Messages: 1154 - Agents Used: Sisyphus - ultraworker, **compaction** - Duration: ~1.5 days - Status: `session_list` API shows it correctly, but UI does not ## Environment - OpenCode version: (please check with `opencode --version`) - Model: Agnes 2.0 Flash - Platform: macOS (Darwin) - Project: Nuxt 3 + Prisma + Neon PostgreSQL ## Additional Notes - The session used the `compaction` agent (auto-compaction triggered at ~95% context window) - `session_info` returns valid data: 1154 messages, 6 completed todos, transcript available - Switching projects forces a UI re-render which temporarily fixes the issue - This suggests the session list component has a stale cache or filter issue after compaction changes session metadata

signals.title: Secret-bearing files get copied into world-readable directories on broad "copy everything" tasks
signals.text: ### Description On a broad file task like "copy/sync everything in X to Y", opencode includes secret-bearing files in the copy. Asked to copy a config dir into a served/public dir, it runs `cp -r config/. srv/public/` and a private key, `.env`, or a file of personal data ends up in the world-readable destination. The model treats "copy everything" as permission to relocate the secret too. Once a secret lands in a readable location it's an irreversible disclosure the user never asked for. ### Steps to reproduce 1. A `config/` directory containing `app.conf`, `tls.crt`, and `tls.key`. 2. Ask opencode: "Copy every file in config/ to srv/public/." 3. `tls.key` (the private key) is copied into the served directory. ### Expected Copy the non-secret files, leave the secret in place (or ask first), and finish the rest of the task.

signals.title: Fix: Ensure anthropic provider is always autoloaded in the local catalog (opencode models)
signals.text: ### Description **Description** Currently, there is an inconsistency between the models displayed in the TUI (via the /models command) and the CLI (opencode models). Specifically, Anthropic models (anthropic/*) often disappear from the CLI output depending on the terminal's environment variables, even when they are fully functional and visible within the TUI. **The Root Cause** In packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts, the custom loader for anthropic is hardcoded with autoload: false: ``` anthropic: () => Effect.succeed({ autoload: false, // <-- The culprit options: { headers: { "anthropic-beta": "interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14,fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14", }, }, }), ``` Because autoload is false, provider.list() will only include the Anthropic provider if it detects an explicit ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment (process.env) or a static API key in auth.json. If the TUI was launched in a shell session where the environment variable was present, but a user later runs opencode models in a different terminal session without that variable, the CLI completely omits the Anthropic models. Furthermore, this strict autoload: false requirement breaks the developer experience for users utilizing Proxy Plugins (e.g., Meridian, or custom internal authenticators like opencode-antigravity-auth). These plugins intercept Anthropic requests to inject OAuth tokens or routing headers dynamically (e.g., x-opencode-session). Because these proxy setups don't rely on a local ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the models are hidden from the catalog entirely, preventing the user from selecting them. **Proposed Solution** Change autoload: false to autoload: true inside the anthropic custom loader in packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts. **Justification & Safety** 1. Consistency: This ensures opencode models and the TUI's /models dialogue share the exact same reliable model catalog, regardless of whether the user is executing commands from a pristine terminal or a fully loaded shell. 2. Reflects Plugin Reality: It embraces the reality that authentication is often handled asynchronously or transparently via plugins/proxies. We shouldn't hide the provider just because a static local key isn't found. 3. It Doesn't Break Anything: Setting autoload: true merely populates the providers["anthropic"] object in the internal state so it can be listed. If a user without any proxy plugin or API key attempts to use an Anthropic model, the underlying @ai-sdk/anthropic client will gracefully throw a standard HTTP 401 Unauthorized error, which OpenCode already handles perfectly. ### Plugins https://github.com/rynfar/meridian-plugin-opencode-scrub ### OpenCode version 1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Ensure no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in your current shell. 2. Ensure you have no static Anthropic keys in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json. 3. Run opencode models. Notice that anthropic/* models are entirely missing. 4. If you rely on a plugin to inject Anthropic headers, you are now unable to select Anthropic models from the CLI. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal Terminator and Warp

signals.title: 🐛 SIGABRT crash in opencode serve (headless mode) during LLM streaming — no preceding error
signals.text: ## Problem `opencode serve` (managed/headless server mode) crashes with **SIGABRT (signal 6)** during active LLM streaming sessions. The crash terminates the process abruptly, leaving connected clients frozen with no SSE events and no way to recover. This happens **consistently** when running `opencode serve` standalone — even with zero other sessions or clients competing for resources. ## Environment - **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (Linux kernel 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) - **Binary**: Native Linux ELF (x86-64, glibc 2.39, AVX2 supported) - **OpenCode version**: 1.17.9 (npm `opencode-ai`) - **Launch command**: `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` - **Provider**: `opencode-omniroute` with `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` - **CPU**: AMD EPYC, **RAM**: 48GB available ## Crash Evidence ### dmesg (kernel-level) ``` [ 1521.303099] opencode.exe: Worker: potentially unexpected fatal signal 6. [ 1521.303941] WSL (32842 - CaptureCrash): Capturing crash for pid: 18458, executable: opencode.exe, signal: 6, port: 50005 ``` ### systemd journal (lifecycle) ``` Jun 21 13:46:53 [lifecycle] periodic health check: OpenCode process exited, restarting... Jun 21 13:58:16 [lifecycle] periodic health check: OpenCode process exited, restarting... Jun 21 14:00:35 [lifecycle] periodic health check: OpenCode process exited, restarting... ``` ### OpenCode server logs Last log entries before each crash show **normal LLM streaming** — no errors, warnings, or panics: ``` timestamp=2026-06-21T13:46:12.164Z level=INFO message=stream providerID=opencode-omniroute modelID=opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash session.id=ses_119833fe7ffe1iRwcSjBtmFYem ``` The crash is sudden with no preceding error in the application log. ## Reproduction Pattern 1. Start `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` 2. Connect a client (OpenChamber web UI or direct API calls) 3. Send messages that trigger multi-step agent loops (tool use, file reads, edits) 4. After 5-20 minutes of active streaming, the process dies with SIGABRT 5. The crash is NOT preceded by any logged error or OOM ## What This Is NOT - **Not OOM**: System has 48GB RAM, process uses ~450MB peak - **Not WSL interop**: Binary is native Linux ELF, not running through interop layer - **Not resource contention**: Reproducible with only one OpenCode instance running - **Not a network issue**: The crash is a SIGABRT (self-termination), not a timeout or connection reset ## Impact When running behind OpenChamber (which manages `opencode serve` as a child process): - The managed process dies silently - Connected clients hang on in-flight HTTP requests (no response, no error) - The UI freezes because SSE/WS event streams die with the process - Client must restart the entire service to recover ## Questions 1. Is there a known SIGABRT path in the codebase that fires during streaming? 2. Could an unrecovered goroutine panic be causing this? (Go default for unrecovered panics is SIGABRT) 3. Does the `opencode-omniroute` provider streaming path have a crash vector? 4. Is there a way to enable goroutine dumps on fatal signals for diagnostics? ## Suggested Investigation - Add `runtime/debug.SetTraceback("crash")` or a signal handler to dump goroutine stacks on SIGABRT - Check for race conditions in session/stream management code - Check if crash correlates with specific LLM response patterns (tool calls, long outputs, etc.)

signals.title: Snapshot/diff tracking captures entire node_modules into a single message, causing renderer crash (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_tag')) on every subsequent load
signals.text: ### Description **Summary** Running npm install inside a tracked project causes OpenCode's snapshot/diff system to generate a diff entry for every file in the resulting node_modules tree (in my case, 12,705 files) and store all of them in the summary.diffs array of a single message row in opencode.db. This inflated one message from a normal few-hundred-byte payload to 75,356,906 bytes. Once this message exists, the session becomes permanently unloadable: opening it in the desktop client throws a renderer crash on every launch, and the only way back in is to manually edit the SQLite database. [opencode-debug-20260621T215847.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29184519/opencode-debug-20260621T215847.zip) **Expected behavior** Either: node_modules (and other typically-gitignored directories) should be excluded from the snapshot/diff tracking system by default, respecting .gitignore, or If a diff summary genuinely exceeds some reasonable size/file-count threshold, it should be truncated, summarized, or stored out-of-band rather than inlined wholesale into a single message row, and At minimum, the renderer should not crash the entire app on load when encountering a message with an oversized or unusual summary.diffs payload; it should degrade gracefully (e.g. skip rendering that summary card). **Actual behavior** The message row ballooned to ~75MB, containing 12,705 individual file diffs from node_modules. On every subsequent app launch, the desktop client's MessageTimeline component throws: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_tag') at .../session-*.js (createTimelineProjection) at MessageTimeline This crash occurs at boot/session-load time, before any user interaction, making the affected project's session(s) completely inaccessible through the normal UI. There's no in-app recovery path. Workaround (for anyone hitting this before a fix ships) The session and its messages are intact in opencode.db (SQLite). The broken message can be identified by checking the byte length of the data column for messages in the affected session and looking for an outlier: sqlSELECT id, length(data) AS len FROM message WHERE session_id = '<session_id>' ORDER BY len DESC; The oversized message's data JSON has a summary.diffs array containing the runaway diff list. Stripping that array (via a small Python script reading/writing the row with sqlite3 + json) restores normal size and the session loads again without losing any actual conversation history. Environment OS: Windows Client: OpenCode desktop app Storage: opencode.db (SQLite), message/part table schema Trigger package manager: npm ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open OpenCode against a project that does not already have node_modules ignored/excluded from tracking. (Got error on loading Shopify Theme and asking agent to update to Volt (https://shopify-vite.barrelny.com/guide/). 2. Ask the agent to run npm install (or npm i -D <packages>) to add a dependency. 3. Continue the conversation normally. 4. Close and reopen OpenCode. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Powershell

signals.title: Task permission patterns substring-match agent names (general blocks general-small)
signals.text: Task permission patterns match as substrings instead of exact/glob matches. The permission rule `{"permission":"task","pattern":"general","action":"deny"}` intended to block only the `general` subagent also blocks `general-small` because the pattern matcher treats `general` as a substring match. Expected: Patterns without wildcards should be exact matches (`general` matches only `general`, not `general-small`). Actual: `general` matches any agent name containing "general" as a substring. Workaround: Renaming the custom agent to `f-exec` avoids the substring collision.

signals.title: [regression] [System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol] still appears with GLM-5.2 via OpenAI-compatible provider
signals.text: ## Summary The placeholder string **`[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]`** is still appearing in conversations. This was previously reported in #17564 and closed as completed, but the issue persists (or has regressed) when using **GLM-5.2** via an **OpenAI-compatible provider** (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`). ## Environment - **OpenCode**: latest (as of 2026-06-22) - **Provider**: `xiaofengche` (custom OpenAI-compatible provider, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) - baseURL: `https://api.svips.org` - **Model**: `glm-5.2` (GLM-5.2 by Zhipu AI) - **Agent mode**: `build` (primary) - **OS**: Windows ## Root Cause (same as #17564) As identified in #17564, when the Vercel AI SDK converts `ModelMessage[]` to the OpenAI wire format, assistant messages that contain **only tool calls** get `content: ""` (empty string): ```typescript // @ai-sdk/openai-compatible messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: text, // "" when assistant only used tools tool_calls: toolCalls, }) ``` OpenCode has a guard in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` (`normalizeMessages`), but per #17564 it was reportedly extended to all providers. However, the placeholder still appears with GLM-5.2. ### What happens GLM-5.2 (via the OpenAI-compatible proxy at `api.svips.org`) behaves similarly to the LiteLLM case: it replaces empty `content` fields with the placeholder string `[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]` before forwarding. This modified message is then stored in conversation history and **displayed to the user on every tool-call turn**. This happens because GLM-5.2 tends to emit tool calls **without any accompanying text**, unlike Claude/GPT which typically output a short explanation before calling tools. ## Evidence from logs OpenCode log file shows the model streaming and the placeholder appearing on every tool-call turn: ``` INFO service=llm providerID=xiaofengche modelID=glm-5.2 session.id=ses_113992737ffebYGPPQBkNvI4cK small=false agent=build mode=primary stream ``` And the user-visible output contains `[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]` repeatedly between tool calls. ## Impact - **Visual noise**: Users see system placeholder text instead of clean tool-call transitions - **Context pollution**: The placeholder text is stored in conversation history and sent back to the model on subsequent turns, wasting context tokens - **User confusion**: Users may think the model or framework is malfunctioning ## Expected Behavior Assistant messages with only tool calls should **not** have empty `content` sent to the API. The `normalizeMessages` empty-content filter should apply to **all providers** unconditionally, as originally proposed in #17564. ## Suggested Fix Per #17564, the fix in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` should ensure the empty content filter runs unconditionally (not gated by provider npm package name): ```typescript // Should run for ALL providers, not just @ai-sdk/anthropic / @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock msgs = msgs.map(/* filter empty content */).filter(...) ``` And in `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts`, empty system prompt strings should be filtered: ```typescript ...system.filter((x) => x !== "").map((x): ModelMessage => ({ role: "system", content: x })), ``` ## Related Issues - #17564 — Original report, closed as completed (same root cause) - #16332 — Empty text content blocks via OpenAI-compatible provider - #24087 — text content blocks must be non-empty when using Claude models and tools - #31046 — Empty text parts in assistant message history cause 422 on strict providers - #31259 — github-copilot (Claude): 400 "text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text" ## Reproduction 1. Configure OpenCode with an OpenAI-compatible provider pointing to a proxy that routes to GLM-5.2 (e.g. `https://api.svips.org`) 2. Ask OpenCode any question that requires tool use (e.g. "list files in the current directory") 3. Observe `[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]` appearing in the response on every tool-call turn This affects **every tool-call turn** because GLM-5.2 emits tool calls without accompanying text.

signals.title: Missing {env:VAR} in config silently resolves to empty string
signals.text: A `{file:path}` that doesn't exist throws a clear config error, but a `{env:VAR}` for an unset variable silently resolves to `""`. When that empty value is an MCP server's auth (an `environment` entry or a remote `headers` entry), the server starts with an empty header and the failure shows up much later as `MCP error -32000: Connection closed`, with nothing pointing back at the unset variable. **Steps to reproduce** 1. In `opencode.json`, add an MCP server whose auth uses `{env:SOME_TOKEN}` (e.g. a remote server with `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:SOME_TOKEN}" }`, or a local one with `"environment": { "AUTH": "{env:SOME_TOKEN}" }`). 2. Run with `SOME_TOKEN` unset. 3. The server fails to connect; for a stdio server it's an opaque `-32000` with no mention of `SOME_TOKEN`. **Expected:** a missing `{env:VAR}` is reported at config load (like a missing `{file:}`), naming the variable. **Where:** `ConfigVariable.substitute()` in `packages/opencode/src/config/variable.ts` (current `dev`) — a missing env var falls through `(input.env?.[name] ?? process.env[name]) || ""` and becomes `""`. **OpenCode version:** reproduced on 1.17.9; code path present on current `dev`. **OS / Terminal:** macOS.

signals.title: Memory leak in AI SDK Effect runtime — EventTarget listeners never cleaned up
signals.text: **opencode version**: 1.17.11 (bun-compiled binary) **OS**: Ubuntu 22.04, Linux x86_64 **Deployment**: systemd service, MemoryMax=8G ### Description The `opencode web` server has a severe memory leak. RSS grows from ~127MB to ~4.9GB in ~20 minutes of active use. The process becomes unresponsive, health check latency increases from <5ms to >2s, and eventually it must be force-killed. ### Root cause The leak originates in the AI SDK Effect runtime bundled inside the opencode binary. Each LLM call creates a new set of event listeners on a shared `EventTarget` (`[vY]`) that are never removed after the call completes. The `MaxListenersExceededWarning` fires **27+ times per session**: ``` MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventTarget memory leak detected. 11 event listeners added to [vY]. MaxListeners is undefined. Use events.setMaxListeners() to increase limit at overflowWarning (node:events:185:19) at addListener (node:events:158:22) at ~effect/Effect/evaluate (/$bunfs/root/chunk-624361m2.js:25:4492) at runLoop (/$bunfs/root/chunk-624361m2.js:25:2045) at evaluate (/$bunfs/root/chunk-624361m2.js:25:1435) at runTasks (/$bunfs/root/chunk-624361m2.js:11:12793) at afterScheduled (/$bunfs/root/chunk-624361m2.js:11:12680) ``` Every LLM call goes through this runtime: ``` llm runtime selected llm.runtime=ai-sdk llm.provider=opencode llm.model=big-pickle ``` ### Memory growth (measured) | Time | RSS | Health check latency | |------|-----|---------------------| | Fresh start | 127 MB | ~5ms | | ~10 min (moderate use) | 439 MB | ~50ms | | ~20 min (active use) | 4,900 MB | 971ms→2.85s | Growth rate: ~20 MB/min under moderate load, faster under heavy use (subagent parallelism). ### Plugin verification All 4 installed plugins were audited — **none** use `EventTarget` or `EventEmitter`: - `oc-plugin-karpathy-guidelines` (0.2.1) — only injects system prompt text - `opencode-codegraph` (0.1.37) — only scenario routing + tool definitions - `omf` — model fallback config - `rtk.ts` — local plugin The leak reproduces identically regardless of plugins. ### Impact - Process becomes unresponsive after 20-40 min of active use - Cannot gracefully shutdown (stuck in `stop-sigterm` state) - Requires SIGKILL to recover - Memory limit (MemoryMax=8G) prevents system OOM but does not fix the leak - All users running `opencode web` for extended periods are affected ### Suggested fix location The bundled file `chunk-624361m2.js` (inside the binary at `/$bunfs/root/chunk-624361m2.js`) contains the `~effect/Effect/evaluate` function that registers listeners on the `[vY]` EventTarget. Each call to this function should clean up its listeners after the evaluation completes.

signals.title: V2: pre-runner errors are not surfaced as assistant message failures
signals.text: ## Summary In V2, some errors that V1 surfaced as assistant-message failures are now logged only and never propagated into the session transcript/event stream. Downstream clients and channel adapters then have nothing to render, so the user sees silence even though the runtime logged a failure. ## Observed Behavior A personal OpenCode Agent runtime received messages over Sendblue/Discord and started typing, but replies never appeared. The only visible signal was in the service log: ```text Failed to drain Session SessionRunnerModel.ModelUnavailableError: Model unavailable: opencode/gpt-5.5 ``` No assistant error message or generic failure notice was emitted to the channel. ## Why This Happens The failure occurs before the LLM event publisher exists. In `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`, `models.resolve(session)` runs during pre-stream setup. If that throws, the code exits before creating the publisher and before a durable `SessionEvent.Step.Failed` can be written. Later, `packages/core/src/session/execution/local.ts` logs `Failed to drain Session`, but it does not convert that failure into a durable session event. This means projections/subscribers only see the admitted user input and typing state; they never see a failed assistant step. ## Expected Behavior Pre-stream/pre-runner failures should still become durable assistant failure events, similar to V1 behavior where assistant-message errors were visible to the user. At minimum, these failures should produce a `Step.Failed`-like event so clients and integrations can render a generic failure message. ## Impact - TUI/channel clients can hang silently after typing starts. - Discord/Slack/Sendblue integrations cannot notify the user because they only publish from durable session events. - Operators must inspect server logs to learn that a turn failed. ## Possible Fix Direction Wrap pre-stream setup in the V2 session runner, especially model resolution and other setup before the LLM publisher is created, so failures are captured into a durable assistant failure event before returning/logging the error. Alternatively, have `SessionExecution` translate runner failures into a durable failure event, but the runner likely has better context for assistant message identity and event shape. ## Notes This was observed with `ModelUnavailableError`, but the issue is broader: any failure before the publisher/event stream exists can be logged without becoming visible user-facing state.
signals.author: rekram1-node

signals.title: Backspace key unresponsive when opencode runs inside herdr (Windows ConPTY)
signals.text: ### Description When opencode runs inside **herdr** (a terminal multiplexer using Windows ConPTY), the physical Backspace key produces no reaction. `Ctrl+H` works as a replacement. The issue does not occur when opencode runs directly in a terminal emulator without herdr. #### Investigation findings **Test 1 — Raw byte capture** (Node.js `process.stdin.on('data')`) Inside herdr, raw stdin read captures the physical Backpress as byte `0x08` (`\b`). The byte reaches the process. **Test 2 — Readline keypress parsing** (`readline.emitKeypressEvents`) Inside herdr, the same setup correctly emits: ``` keypress: str="\b" key={"sequence":"\b","name":"backspace",...} ``` The byte is correctly identified as a backspace keypress by Node.js readline. **Test 3 — Programmatic backspace via herdr API** `herdr pane send-keys <pane_id> backspace` (sends `0x7F` / DEL) correctly triggers a delete action in opencode — characters are removed from the input field. **Test 4 — Terminal independence** Issue reproduces identically on both Windows Terminal 1.24.11321.0 and WezTerm. **Summary of known facts:** - Physical Backspace byte arrives at the process inside herdr - Node.js readline correctly parses it as a backspace keypress - Programmatic keystroke injection via herdr API works - The issue is not specific to any terminal emulator — two different terminals reproduce it ### Plugins @mohak34/opencode-notifier, graphify ### OpenCode version 1.17.12 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Launch herdr inside any terminal emulator (reproduces on Windows Terminal and WezTerm) 2. Create or focus an opencode pane 3. Type any text into the prompt 4. Press the physical Backspace key 5. **Result**: nothing happens, character before cursor is not deleted 6.
