signals.title: fix(core): steer manual compaction by default
signals.text: ## What A manual `/compact` during an active turn now runs at the next step boundary instead of silently waiting for the whole turn — and any queued prompts — to finish. `Session.compact` supported steer delivery all along, but defaulted to `"queue"`, and no client ever passed `delivery`. This flips the default to `"steer"` so user-initiated compaction means "compact soon", not "compact after all queued work". ## Before / After **Before**: `/compact` during a long tool-heavy turn admits a `delivery:"queue"` compaction row. Queue rows are invisible at step boundaries (`runPendingCompaction(sessionID, "steer")` only sees the steer lane), so nothing happens until the turn goes idle — and if a queued prompt was enqueued earlier, the compaction waits behind that entire turn too. The user sees no `Compaction.Started` for the rest of the run and no indication of when it will fire. **After**: `/compact` admits a steer-delivery row. At the next step boundary the runner consumes it ahead of queued prompts, requests the summary, and continues the turn (if steps remain) inside the compacted context. Explicit `delivery: "queue"` keeps the old parking behavior. ## How - `packages/core/src/session.ts`: `Session.compact` default delivery `"queue"` → `"steer"`. - `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`: `runSteps` restructured so every step boundary has one shape — control items first, then a single exit decision, then the model call. The turn continues only while the first step, a continuation, or steer input is owed; deciding after control items means consuming the last steered compaction ends the turn instead of issuing an input-free model call. The drain loop then picks up any queued work. - `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts`: endpoint description updated (no generated client changes; verified `bun run generate` in `packages/client` is a no-op). Ordering semantics are unchanged: enqueue order rules the steer lane, and the compaction row is a barrier. Steers admitted before `/compact` get one more step (so the summary reflects them); steers admitted after it deliver into the fresh compacted epoch. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant I as SessionInbox (steer lane) participant R as SessionRunner participant M as Model R->>M: step N (in flight) U->>I: steer "actually do X" U->>I: /compact (steer, barrier) M-->>R: step N settles R->>I: promote steers up to barrier R->>M: step N+1 (sees "actually do X") M-->>R: step N+1 settles R->>I: consume compaction barrier R->>M: summary request R->>M: continuation in compacted context ``` ## Scope - No TUI/ACP call-site changes needed: they omit `delivery` and inherit the new default. - No change to queued-compaction semantics (`delivery: "queue"` still parks behind earlier queued prompts, per the existing drain-boundary tests). - No hard `compact > steer` priority: a compaction never jumps ahead of steers enqueued before it. That's deliberate — enqueue order stays the single ordering law. ## Testing From `packages/core`: - `bun run test -- test/session-runner.test.ts` — 158 pass, including two new tests: - steer compaction admitted mid-turn runs at the boundary before queued prompts, with an exact request count proving no input-free model call after the barrier - steer compaction admitted mid-tool-turn runs before the turn's continuation step - `bun run test -- test/session-compact.test.ts test/session-prompt.test.ts test/session-execution.test.ts test/session-projector.test.ts test/session-compaction.test.ts` — 80 pass - `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` and `packages/protocol` Existing coverage updated: the default-delivery assertion now expects `steer` (with a new explicit-queue assertion), and the queued-compaction ordering test passes `delivery: "queue"` explicitly.

signals.title: fix(core): avoid deep cloning session parts
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Fixes #35107 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `Session.updatePart` currently deep-clones every part before publishing it. Large text, reasoning, and tool-output strings are immutable, so deep-cloning duplicates the entire payload while Bun may retain the allocator pages after the temporary copy is released. Repeated updates can therefore make server RSS grow far beyond the live session data. This keeps the event payload isolated from later top-level mutation with a shallow copy while reusing immutable output strings. It preserves the existing event-copy contract without copying large payloads. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added a regression assertion that mutating the input part after `updatePart` does not change the published event. - Ran `bun test test/session/session.test.ts test/session/processor-effect.test.ts` from `packages/opencode`: 24 passed, 0 failed. - Ran `bun typecheck` from `packages/opencode`. - The pre-push hook ran the repository typecheck: 30 tasks passed. ### Screenshots / recordings n/a ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(app): speed up cold home navigation
signals.text: ## The symptom Desktop Home navigation looked bimodal with real Beta data. - A warm tab-to-Home click stabilized in about `86 ms`. - The first click after idling in a session stabilized in `495-639 ms`, with a `618 ms` median across five runs. The difference was the Home query cache. Once the cached query had been collected, Home fetched the entire server session inventory before Solid could commit the route. The traced account had: - `5,241` total sessions - `1,799` root sessions - `64` rendered Home rows ## Following the slow click The old cold path was: ```text session tab teardown -> GET all sessions, page 1 -> GET all sessions, page 2 -> discard children and archived sessions in App -> reconcile the large query result into Solid -> render 64 rows -> sort the retained session store twice per row -> rebuild request trees twice per row ``` The key observation was that the existing generic session API already supports `parentID=null`. Home was paying to transfer every child session only to remove it immediately in [`parseHomeSessionIndex`](packages/app/src/context/global-sync/home-session-index.ts). No Core, Server, Protocol, migration, or generated-client change is needed. ## Paired live-server experiment I issued alternating requests against the unchanged running Beta server so both query shapes saw the same service load. | Query | Median | Range | Rows | Payload | Pages | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Current Home: all sessions | 683 ms | 536-850 ms | 5,241 | 2.56 MB | 2 | | App-only: `parentID=null` | 316 ms | 241-361 ms | 1,799 | 816 KB | 1 | That is a `54%` reduction in API completion time and a `68%` reduction in payload size using the existing public API. Home still applies its existing archive filter locally. There is deliberately no new archive query parameter or generated OpenAPI churn in this PR. ## The Solid scaling problem The network request was not the only data-dependent cost. Every visible Home row creates permission and question status computations. Before this change: - Each computation called `data.session.list()`. - `session.list()` performed `Object.values(...).toSorted(...)` every time. - Each request lookup rebuilt a parent-to-children map over the entire retained session store. With 64 rows, that can become 128 complete sorts and 128 complete tree builds on each Home mount. Focused benchmarks over `5,238` real sessions measured: | Work | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | 128 ordered `session.list()` reads | 23-37 ms | about 0.02 ms | | 128 request-tree scans | 28-44 ms | 2-3 ms | ## What changed ### Ask for root sessions [`home-session-index.ts`](packages/app/src/context/global-sync/home-session-index.ts) now includes `parentID=null` on every cursor request. The existing local root/archive filter remains because locally remembered sessions are merged into the fetched index. ### Keep unfiltered Home server-wide Unfiltered Home now displays root sessions from the entire focused server, including sessions whose directories are not in the added-project list. [`home-session-records.ts`](packages/app/src/pages/home/home-session-records.ts) creates display metadata for those rows while preserving the session's actual directory. Explicit project selection still filters locally. A stale selected directory also remains scoped instead of falling back to the server-wide list. ### Keep large query data opaque to Solid [`home-sessions-controller.tsx`](packages/app/src/pages/home/home-sessions-controller.tsx) returns the immutable query result through an accessor. This prevents Solid Query from recursively unwrapping every session while mounting Home. ### Memoize session ordering [`client/src/solid/data.ts`](packages/client/src/solid/data.ts) memoizes the sorted session array. Ordering and reactivity stay the same, but repeated readers no longer copy and sort the full store. ### Scope Home attention checks [`project-avatar-state.ts`](packages/app/src/pages/layout/project-avatar-state.ts) uses the client's existing family index for known-root Home rows. Other tab and composer callers retain the existing global descendant behavior. ## Product behavior - Unfiltered Home: all active root sessions from the focused server. - Selected project: only that project's worktree and sandboxes. - Unadded directory: row remains visible and opens the session's actual directory. - Archived and child sessions: remain hidden as before. - Generic API behavior: unchanged. ## Validation - Production Electron renderer build - App Home pagination and projection tests - App and Client package typechecks - Real-data paired API benchmark against the unchanged Beta service - Real-data Solid hot-path benchmarks ## Follow-up The isolated Desktop profiling harness exposed a separate development lifecycle issue: Electron closed while its private `serve --service` Bun process remained, leaving the parent command waiting. That should be investigated separately from this PR.

signal.title: refactor(desktop): move IPC to Effect RPC
signal.text: ## Summary - replace the desktop's `ipcMain.handle` / `ipcRenderer.invoke` channel wiring with an Effect 4 RPC contract over MsgPack-framed `MessagePort`s - define one PascalCase `Rpc.make(...)` object per operation and event stream, using each object’s `_tag` as the only wire name - split contracts and handler layers into app, storage, file, window, menu, updater, and WSL capability groups, then compose them into `DesktopRpcs` - omit payloads for zero-input RPCs and use named object payloads for every input-bearing RPC; positional arguments remain only in the compatibility `window.api` facade - derive the preload invoke/send/event facade types from the RPC group while validating every request, response, updater state, WSL state, picker payload, menu action, and binary value through the schemas - reduce preload to a 0.38 kB MessagePort relay plus the native `getPathForFile` bridge; the renderer owns `RpcClient`, its managed runtime, and the compatibility API adapter - hand off a fresh port on every renderer load, isolate connections per `WebContents`, and interrupt only the reloaded window without disturbing other windows - model main-to-renderer notifications as a union of `Schema.TaggedClass` events emitted through one `DesktopEvents` RPC stream, while preserving updater/WSL subscription behavior, picker-token ownership, native translation checks, and sender-targeted window/menu operations - copy binary payloads as `Uint8Array` values on the wire and restore the existing `ArrayBuffer` facade in preload ## Verification - `bun typecheck` in `packages/desktop` - 70 desktop tests passed across 16 files, including new multi-window, reload, binary, and stream transport coverage - the remaining draft-store test cannot load `node:sqlite` in this host Bun runtime (the same environment limitation occurs without this change) - `bun x electron-vite build` built main (`161.93 kB`) and preload (`0.38 kB`); signal.title: [regression] [System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol] still appears with GLM-5.2 via OpenAI-compatible provider
signal.text: ## Summary The placeholder string **`[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]`** is still appearing in conversations. This was previously reported in #17564 and closed as completed, but the issue persists (or has regressed) when using **GLM-5.2** via an **OpenAI-compatible provider** (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`). ## Environment - **OpenCode**: latest (as of 2026-06-22) - **Provider**: `xiaofengche` (custom OpenAI-compatible provider, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) - baseURL: `https://api.svips.org` - **Model**: `glm-5.2` (GLM-5.2 by Zhipu AI) - **Agent mode**: `build` (primary) - **OS**: Windows ## Root Cause (same as #17564) As identified in #17564, when the Vercel AI SDK converts `ModelMessage[]` to the OpenAI wire format, assistant messages that contain **only tool calls** get `content: ""` (empty string): ```typescript // @ai-sdk/openai-compatible messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: text, // "" when assistant only used tools tool_calls: toolCalls, }) ``` OpenCode has a guard in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` (`normalizeMessages`), but per #17564 it was reportedly extended to all providers. However, the placeholder still appears with GLM-5.2. ### What happens GLM-5.2 (via the OpenAI-compatible proxy at `api.svips.org`) behaves similarly to the LiteLLM case: it replaces empty `content` fields with the placeholder string `[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]` before forwarding. This modified message is then stored in conversation history and **displayed to the user on every tool-call turn**. This happens because GLM-5.2 tends to emit tool calls **without any accompanying text**, unlike Claude/GPT which typically output a short explanation before calling tools. ## Evidence from logs OpenCode log file shows the model streaming and the placeholder appearing on every tool-call turn: ``` INFO service=llm providerID=xiaofengche modelID=glm-5.2 session.id=ses_113992737ffebYGPPQBkNvI4cK small=false agent=build mode=primary stream ``` And the user-visible output contains `[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]` repeatedly between tool calls. ## Impact - **Visual noise**: Users see system placeholder text instead of clean tool-call transitions - **Context pollution**: The placeholder text is stored in conversation history and sent back to the model on subsequent turns, wasting context tokens - **User confusion**: Users may think the model or framework is malfunctioning ## Expected Behavior Assistant messages with only tool calls should **not** have empty `content` sent to the API. The `normalizeMessages` empty-content filter should apply to **all providers** unconditionally, as originally proposed in #17564. ## Suggested Fix Per #17564, the fix in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` should ensure the empty content filter runs unconditionally (not gated by provider npm package name): ```typescript // Should run for ALL providers, not just @ai-sdk/anthropic / @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock msgs = msgs.map(/* filter empty content */).filter(...) ``` And in `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts`, empty system prompt strings should be filtered: ```typescript ...system.filter((x) => x !== "").map((x): ModelMessage => ({ role: "system", content: x })), ``` ## Related Issues - #17564 — Original report, closed as completed (same root cause) - #16332 — Empty text content blocks via OpenAI-compatible provider - #24087 — text content blocks must be non-empty when using Claude models and tools - #31046 — Empty text parts in assistant message history cause 422 on strict providers - #31259 — github-copilot (Claude): 400 "text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text" ## Reproduction 1. Configure OpenCode with an OpenAI-compatible provider pointing to a proxy that routes to GLM-5.2 (e.g. `https://api.svips.org`) 2. Ask OpenCode any question that requires tool use (e.g. "list files in the current directory") 3. Observe `[System: Empty message content sanitised to satisfy protocol]` appearing in the response on every tool-call turn This affects **every tool-call turn** because GLM-5.2 emits tool calls without accompanying text.

signal.title: Task permission patterns substring-match agent names (general blocks general-small)
signal.text: Task permission patterns match as substrings instead of exact/glob matches. The permission rule `{"permission":"task","pattern":"general","action":"deny"}` intended to block only the `general` subagent also blocks `general-small` because the pattern matcher treats `general` as a substring match. Expected: Patterns without wildcards should be exact matches (`general` matches only `general`, not `general-small`). Actual: `general` matches any agent name containing "general" as a substring. Workaround: Renaming the custom agent to `f-exec` avoids the substring collision.

signal.title: Snapshot/diff tracking captures entire node_modules into a single message, causing renderer crash (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_tag')) on every subsequent load
signal.text: ### Description **Summary** Running npm install inside a tracked project causes OpenCode's snapshot/diff system to generate a diff entry for every file in the resulting node_modules tree (in my case, 12,705 files) and store all of them in the summary.diffs array of a single message row in opencode.db. This inflated one message from a normal few-hundred-byte payload to 75,356,906 bytes. Once this message exists, the session becomes permanently unloadable: opening it in the desktop client throws a renderer crash on every launch, and the only way back in is to manually edit the SQLite database. [opencode-debug-20260621T215847.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29184519/opencode-debug-20260621T215847.zip) **Expected behavior** Either: node_modules (and other typically-gitignored directories) should be excluded from the snapshot/diff tracking system by default, respecting .gitignore, or If a diff summary genuinely exceeds some reasonable size/file-count threshold, it should be truncated, summarized, or stored out-of-band rather than inlined wholesale into a single message row, and At minimum, the renderer should not crash the entire app on load when encountering a message with an oversized or unusual summary.diffs payload; it should degrade gracefully (e.g. skip rendering that summary card). **Actual behavior** The message row ballooned to ~75MB, containing 12,705 individual file diffs from node_modules. On every subsequent app launch, the desktop client's MessageTimeline component throws: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_tag') at .../session-*.js (createTimelineProjection) at MessageTimeline This crash occurs at boot/session-load time, before any user interaction, making the affected project's session(s) completely inaccessible through the normal UI. There's no in-app recovery path. Workaround (for anyone hitting this before a fix ships) The session and its messages are intact in opencode.db (SQLite). The broken message can be identified by checking the byte length of the data column for messages in the affected session and looking for an outlier: sqlSELECT id, length(data) AS len FROM message WHERE session_id = '<session_id>' ORDER BY len DESC; The oversized message's data JSON has a summary.diffs array containing the runaway diff list. Stripping that array (via a small Python script reading/writing the row with sqlite3 + json) restores normal size and the session loads again without losing any actual conversation history. Environment OS: Windows Client: OpenCode desktop app Storage: opencode.db (SQLite), message/part table schema Trigger package manager: npm ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open OpenCode against a project that does not already have node_modules ignored/excluded from tracking. (Got error on loading Shopify Theme and asking agent to update to Volt (https://shopify-vite.barrelny.com/guide/). 2. Ask the agent to run npm install (or npm i -D <packages>) to add a dependency. 3. Continue the conversation normally. 4. Close and reopen OpenCode. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Powershell

signal.title: Deepseek and MCPs ($ref/$defs in MCP tool schemas causes AttributeError)
signal.text: ### Description **Title**: DeepSeek provider: $ref/$defs in MCP tool schemas causes AttributeError **Description**: **Version**: opencode 1.17.5 **Provider**: DeepSeek Affected MCP servers: Asana (mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp), Notion (@notionhq/notion-mcp-server) **Error:** Error from provider: Error resolving schema reference '#/$defs/richTextRequest': AttributeError("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lookup'") **Possible cause**: MCP servers output valid JSON Schema 2020-12 with $ref → $defs references. DeepSeek's API (like Fireworks, Anthropic, Gemini) strictly validates schemas and rejects unresolved $ref pointers. The same error occurs with Notion MCP (#/properties/sections/items/properties/tasks/items/properties/assignee). **Expected fix**: opencode should dereference/flatten $ref before sending to DeepSeek — similar to the Gemini sanitization done in #12292. Workaround: Disable affected MCP servers or switch to a provider that handles $ref natively (e.g. OpenAI). **References**: - LiteLLM #26692 — identical error with Fireworks - opencode #12292 / #12295 — Gemini fix for same class of problem - FastMCP #2808 — schema dereferencing for MCP client compatibility ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.5 ### Steps to reproduce { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "small_model": "google/gemini-3-flash-preview", "mcp": { "asana": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp", "oauth": { "clientId": "{env:ASANA_MCP_CLIENT_ID}", "clientSecret": "{env:ASANA_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET}" } }, "chrome-devtools": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest"] }, "figma": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "figma-mcp"] }, "notion-sys": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"], "environment": { "NOTION_TOKEN": "xyz" } }, "notion-lv": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"], "environment": { "NOTION_TOKEN": "xyz" } } } } ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System macOS 26.4.1 ### Terminal Nova, System bash

signal.title: Copilot Claude Opus 4.8 assistant prefill 400 after malformed pseudo tool-call text
signal.text: ## Description `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8` can reject a follow-up request with: ```text APIError 400: This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message. isRetryable: false ``` After re-checking local SQLite metadata on OpenCode 1.17.7, this now appears to be downstream of the malformed pseudo tool-call issue in #31247. The observed chain is: 1. Opus 4.8 emits pseudo tool-call text such as `<invoke ...>` as assistant text. 2. The assistant message is still marked `finish=tool-calls`. 3. There is no structured tool part in that assistant message. 4. OpenCode continues the tool loop. 5. The next provider request effectively ends with an assistant message. 6. Copilot Claude rejects that request as unsupported assistant prefill. ## Steps to Reproduce I do not yet have a small deterministic repro, but the failures occurred in normal OpenCode TUI sessions using `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8`: 1. Start an OpenCode TUI session with `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8`. 2. Perform a long tool-heavy task. 3. Continue through multiple automatic tool-call turns. 4. Hit a malformed Opus 4.8 turn where `finish=tool-calls`, there are zero structured tool parts, and the assistant text contains pseudo tool-call markup such as `<invoke ...>`. 5. Observe the next request fail with the assistant-prefill 400. ## Expected Behavior OpenCode should not send a Copilot Claude request whose final message is assistant. More importantly, OpenCode should handle a malformed `finish=tool-calls` response with no actual tool call at the root, instead of continuing the tool loop with an assistant-ending history. ## Actual Behavior The provider rejects the follow-up request with: ```text This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message. ``` Every sampled prefill 400 was immediately preceded by a `claude-opus-4.8` assistant message with this structure: ```text finish: tool-calls structured tool parts: 0 assistant text contains: <invoke ...> ``` Sampled chain: | Error message | Previous message | Previous finish | Previous tool parts | Previous text contains `<invoke>` | |---|---|---|---:|---:| | `msg_ea14109c...` | `msg_ea140d8ac...` | `tool-calls` | 0 | yes | | `msg_ea14ee3d...` | `msg_ea14ec5d...` | `tool-calls` | 0 | yes | | `msg_ea1565f9...` | `msg_ea1562db...` | `tool-calls` | 0 | yes | ## Additional Evidence Downstream symptom evidence: https://gist.github.com/doomsday616/659c12bc0d0f02dff5a605e2ea6ec4cd Root-cause evidence is in #31247: https://gist.github.com/doomsday616/d3fb56acd0f14964a9797df35f1fcd96 Both gists contain only sanitized structural metadata from local SQLite rows. Private message text and local/private identifiers are not included. ## OpenCode Version ```text 1.17.7 ``` ## Operating System ```text Windows 11 ``` ## Terminal ```text Windows Terminal / PowerShell 7 ``` ## Provider / Model ```text github-copilot / claude-opus-4.8 ``` ## Related Issues - #31247 — likely root cause: Opus 4.8 pseudo tool-call text persisted as assistant text while `finish=tool-calls` and no structured tool part exists. - #13768 — same/similar assistant-prefill rejection with GitHub Copilot + Claude Opus. - #19517 — Azure AI Claude via LiteLLM rejects assistant prefill. - #29760 — Bedrock Claude Opus 4.6 rejects assistant prefill. ## Sanitization The original full session contains private content, so I cannot share a raw export publicly. The linked evidence includes only sanitized structural excerpts and provider error metadata.

signal.title: 🐛 SIGABRT crash in opencode serve (headless mode) during LLM streaming — no preceding error
signal.text: ## Problem `opencode serve` (managed/headless server mode) crashes with **SIGABRT (signal 6)** during active LLM streaming sessions. The crash terminates the process abruptly, leaving connected clients frozen with no SSE events and no way to recover. This happens **consistently** when running `opencode serve` standalone — even with zero other sessions or clients competing for resources. ## Environment - **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (Linux kernel 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) - **Binary**: Native Linux ELF (x86-64, glibc 2.39, AVX2 supported) - **OpenCode version**: 1.17.9 (npm `opencode-ai`) - **Launch command**: `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` - **Provider**: `opencode-omniroute` with `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` - **CPU**: AMD EPYC, **RAM**: 48GB available ## Crash Evidence ### dmesg (kernel-level) ``` [ 1521.303099] opencode.exe: Worker: potentially unexpected fatal signal 6. [ 1521.303941] WSL (32842 - CaptureCrash): Capturing crash for pid: 18458, executable: opencode.exe, signal: 6, port: 50005 ``` ### systemd journal (lifecycle) ``` Jun 21 13:46:53 [lifecycle] periodic health check: OpenCode process exited, restarting... Jun 21 13:58:16 [lifecycle] periodic health check: OpenCode process exited, restarting... Jun 21 14:00:35 [lifecycle] periodic health check: OpenCode process exited, restarting... ``` ### OpenCode server logs Last log entries before each crash show **normal LLM streaming** — no errors, warnings, or panics: ``` timestamp=2026-06-21T13:46:12.164Z level=INFO message=stream providerID=opencode-omniroute modelID=opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash session.id=ses_119833fe7ffe1iRwcSjBtmFYem ``` The crash is sudden with no preceding error in the application log. ## Reproduction Pattern 1. Start `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` 2. Connect a client (OpenChamber web UI or direct API calls) 3. Send messages that trigger multi-step agent loops (tool use, file reads, edits) 4. After 5-20 minutes of active streaming, the process dies with SIGABRT 5. The crash is NOT preceded by any logged error or OOM ## What This Is NOT - **Not OOM**: System has 48GB RAM, process uses ~450MB peak - **Not WSL interop**: Binary is native Linux ELF, not running through interop layer - **Not resource contention**: Reproducible with only one OpenCode instance running - **Not a network issue**: The crash is a SIGABRT (self-termination), not a timeout or connection reset ## Impact When running behind OpenChamber (which manages `opencode serve` as a child process): - The managed process dies silently - Connected clients hang on in-flight HTTP requests (no response, no error) - The UI freezes because SSE/WS event streams die with the process - Client must restart the entire service to recover ## Questions 1. Is there a known SIGABRT path in the codebase that fires during streaming? 2. Could an unrecovered goroutine panic be causing this? (Go default for unrecovered panics is SIGABRT) 3. Does the `opencode-omniroute` provider streaming path have a crash vector? 4. Is there a way to enable goroutine dumps on fatal signals for diagnostics? ## Suggested Investigation - Add `runtime/debug.SetTraceback("crash")` or a signal handler to dump goroutine stacks on SIGABRT - Check for race conditions in session/stream management code - Check if crash correlates with specific LLM response patterns (tool calls, long outputs, etc.)

signal.title: Fix: Ensure anthropic provider is always autoloaded in the local catalog (opencode models)
signal.text: ### Description **Description** Currently, there is an inconsistency between the models displayed in the TUI (via the /models command) and the CLI (opencode models). Specifically, Anthropic models (anthropic/*) often disappear from the CLI output depending on the terminal's environment variables, even when they are fully functional and visible within the TUI. **The Root Cause** In packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts, the custom loader for anthropic is hardcoded with autoload: false: ``` anthropic: () => Effect.succeed({ autoload: false, // <-- The culprit options: { headers: { "anthropic-beta": "interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14,fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14", }, }, }), ``` Because autoload is false, provider.list() will only include the Anthropic provider if it detects an explicit ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment (process.env) or a static API key in auth.json. If the TUI was launched in a shell session where the environment variable was present, but a user later runs opencode models in a different terminal session without that variable, the CLI completely omits the Anthropic models. Furthermore, this strict autoload: false requirement breaks the developer experience for users utilizing Proxy Plugins (e.g., Meridian, or custom internal authenticators like opencode-antigravity-auth). These plugins intercept Anthropic requests to inject OAuth tokens or routing headers dynamically (e.g., x-opencode-session). Because these proxy setups don't rely on a local ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the models are hidden from the catalog entirely, preventing the user from selecting them. **Proposed Solution** Change autoload: false to autoload: true inside the anthropic custom loader in packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts. **Justification & Safety** 1. Consistency: This ensures opencode models and the TUI's /models dialogue share the exact same reliable model catalog, regardless of whether the user is executing commands from a pristine terminal or a fully loaded shell. 2. Reflects Plugin Reality: It embraces the reality that authentication is often handled asynchronously or transparently via plugins/proxies. We shouldn't hide the provider just because a static local key isn't found. 3. It Doesn't Break Anything: Setting autoload: true merely populates the providers["anthropic"] object in the internal state so it can be listed. If a user without any proxy plugin or API key attempts to use an Anthropic model, the underlying @ai-sdk/anthropic client will gracefully throw a standard HTTP 401 Unauthorized error, which OpenCode already handles perfectly. ### Plugins https://github.com/rynfar/meridian-plugin-opencode-scrub ### OpenCode version 1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Ensure no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in your current shell. 2. Ensure you have no static Anthropic keys in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json. 3. Run opencode models. Notice that anthropic/* models are entirely missing. 4. If you rely on a plugin to inject Anthropic headers, you are now unable to select Anthropic models from the CLI. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal Terminator and Warp

signal.text: ### Description On a broad file task like "copy/sync everything in X to Y", opencode includes secret-bearing files in the copy. signal.title: sampledChecksum() skips the last ~2KB of content, causing stale file caches
signal.text: ### Description `sampledChecksum()` in `packages/core/src/util/encode.ts` (line 42) uses `content.length - size` as the last sampling point. The window is centered on each point and clamped to `[0, content.length - size]`, so the last window covers `[content.length - 6144, content.length - 2048]` — the final ~2KB of the content is never hashed. This function is used as a cache key in `packages/ui/src/components/file.tsx` (line 1089) and `packages/app/src/pages/session/file-tabs.tsx` (line 202). Edits to the end of a large file (>500KB) produce the same cache key, so the UI shows stale content. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a file larger than 500KB in the TUI 2. Edit the last few lines of the file 3. The file viewer cache key does not change because the last 2KB is excluded from the sampled checksum 4. The UI continues showing the pre-edit content ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal N/A

signal.title: File Tree Cache Persists After Folder Deletion
signal.text: ### Description Application: opencode-desktop v1.17.3 (Electron 42.3.3) OS: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04) Issue: File tree component displays "Failed to list files" toasts for folders that no longer exist on disk. Description After creating and then deleting a folder (apps/asalkita2) within an opencode Desktop workspace, the file tree UI continues to show error toasts for subdirectories inside that deleted folder. The cache appears to be stored in a location that survives: Deleting the folder from disk Deleting the entire .config/ai.opencode.desktop/ directory Restarting the opencode desktop application process Rebooting the machine Steps to Reproduce Create a folder in the workspace: mkdir -p apps/test-Project/static/promotion-media1/{mobile,desktop} Open opencode Desktop and expand the folder in the file tree Close opencode Desktop Delete the folder: rm -rf apps/test-Project Reopen opencode Desktop Observe error toasts for apps/test-Project/static/promotion-media1/mobile and desktop Expected Behavior The file tree should reflect the current filesystem state. Deleted folders should not appear in the tree nor cause errors. Actual Behavior The file tree shows "Failed to list files" toasts for paths inside the deleted folder. The cache is read when the renderer requests directory listings, even though the paths don't exist. Investigation Notes The error comes from FileSystem.list() in the opencode server process The cache is not in: SQLite database (opencode.db), git snapshot, or Chromium Local Storage The opencode.global.dat only stores fileTree: {opened, width, tab} — NOT expanded directory state The cache appears to be embedded in the bundled app.asar or stored in an unidentified internal location Workaround (Temporary) Creating empty placeholder directories for the cached paths silences the errors: mkdir -p apps/fe/{tests,static/{samples,promotion-media1/{mobile,desktop}}} Additional Info This is not the first opencode Desktop issue we've encountered with persistent file tree state storage. Related debugging revealed that the file tree expanded/collapsed state does not appear to be persistently stored in any obvious location, yet the deleted folder's structure continues to be "seen" by the server. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: OpenAI Responses (gpt-5.5): 500 server_error doom-loop when too many tools are enabled
signal.text: ### Summary When many tools are enabled (e.g. several MCP servers), opencode sends every tool definition in a single OpenAI Responses request. The ChatGPT/Codex OAuth backend rejects requests carrying too many tools with a generic 500 `server_error`. Because the retry policy has no attempt cap for 5xx, opencode then retries the same oversized request indefinitely — turning it into a multi-hour doom-loop that makes the model (e.g. gpt-5.5) effectively unusable. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a setup with a large number of enabled tools (many MCP servers — ~870 tool definitions in my case). 2. Use an `@ai-sdk/openai` model on the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth path (e.g. gpt-5.5). 3. Send any prompt that triggers a model turn. ### Expected The request succeeds, or fails with an actionable error. ### Actual The backend returns a 500 `server_error` and opencode retries the identical request with no cap, looping for hours. ### Notes on root cause - Reproduced with 876 tool definitions: 5 `server_error`s and a stuck loop. The same prompt with `--pure` (11 tools) works, confirming tool **count** is the trigger — not schema, request size, or reasoning threading. - The retry policy applies to 5xx with no max-attempt cap, which amplifies the single rejection into the loop. ### Environment - Model: gpt-5.5 (OpenAI Responses, ChatGPT/Codex OAuth) - Runtime: AI-SDK path (`@ai-sdk/openai`)

signal.title: Import sessions after runtime change to rust does not work
signal.text: ### Description Assume you have exported a session to json file, using version 1.15.4. When you trying to import this version in a new opencode, for example 1.17.8 it will fail and print unrelated message like "file not found" I ask opencode to try to research the issue and it found that previous version exported file in Utf16-LE format that newest version cannot read (only Utf-8 supported) Here is AI reply: `The session imported successfully after converting to UTF-8 without BOM. The opencode import command (1.17.8) uses a Rust binary that expects UTF-8 without BOM and fails with a misleading "File not found" error when it can't decode the file. Fix: Convert the file to UTF-8 (without BOM): $content = Get-Content -LiteralPath "ses_1bf8a86b1ffeNAd6lVyuCurdUt.json" -Raw [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText("ses_utf8.json", $content, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)) opencode import ses_utf8.json The session format itself (1.15.4) was compatible with 1.17.8 import — only the encoding was the issue.` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.8 ### Steps to reproduce 1. export any session using version 1.15.4 to a json file 2. try to import the session with the latest version ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows terminal

signal.title: [BUG] Feishu plugin: orphaned sessions continue looping after abort, causing sustained high CPU
signal.text: ## Problem When a Feishu (飞书) session is **aborted** by the user (e.g., via cancel in the Feishu UI), the session is marked as `orphan=true` but its processing **loop is not terminated**. The opencode process continues to re-enter the loop (`step=0 → step=1 → ...`), making repeated LLM inference requests indefinitely. If the parent terminal/process exits, the opencode main process becomes an orphan (PPID=1) and **keeps consuming high CPU** (observed 370-420% CPU, ~8.5GB RSS) with no way to stop it except manually killing the process. ## Root Cause The Feishu plugin's `session.error` handler logs `orphan=true` but does **not** properly clean up the session's pending tasks or prevent the session from re-entering the processing loop. This is distinct from the existing orphan session issues (#19023, #30683, #31787) which deal with DB records or project ID drift — this is specifically about the **Feishu WebSocket channel** triggering repeated loop restarts for aborted sessions. Additionally, when the Feishu WebSocket connection drops (e.g., certificate verification errors), the reconnect logic may trigger re-processing of orphaned sessions. ## Reproduction 1. Start opencode with Feishu plugin configured 2. Send a message from Feishu to trigger a session 3. Cancel/abort the session from the Feishu UI 4. Observe that the session is marked `orphan=true` but continues looping 5. Close the terminal running opencode 6. The opencode process becomes orphaned (PPID=1) and continues consuming high CPU ## Observed Logs ``` level=ERROR message=process session.id=ses_xxx error=Aborted stack=undefined level=WARN message="[feishu] 收到 session.error 事件" sessionId=ses_xxx errMsg=Aborted orphan=true level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_xxx step=0 // <-- loop restarts despite orphan=true level=INFO message=stream providerID=omlx modelID=Qwen3___5-122B-A10B-4bit session.id=ses_xxx ``` ## Expected Behavior When a session is aborted and marked as orphan, the Feishu plugin should: 1. Remove the session from the active processing queue 2. Not allow the session to re-enter the loop on subsequent iterations 3. Clean up any pending message handlers for that session ## Environment - Opencode version: 1.17.8 - Platform: macOS ARM64 (Darwin) - Model: oMLX local (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-4bit) - Feishu plugin: WebSocket mode (persistent connection) ## Related Issues - #19023 — Sessions permanently stuck after server restart or stream interruption - #31787 — Effect.orDie orphans subagent sessions after tool error - #20099 — Runtime watchdog for stuck tool/session recovery - #22542 — Feishu media type error - #27642 — Feishu locale routing issue

See: #29584 Additionally, I have found that the environment information and the skills list in the system prompt also affect the cache hit rate. Currently, the environment information in the system prompt includes: model id & provider, working directory, workspace root folder, git repo flag, platform, today's date. Below is my analysis of each field's impact on cache hits: - ✅ **model id & provider:** It only changes when switching models, and different models have different KV caches, so switching models naturally leads to cache misses. So this field is fine. - ✅ **working directory:** Once a session is created, this field does not change dynamically, and it is information the LLM needs to know. - ✅ **platform:** This field is stable, would not change during the lifetime of a session, and is also information the LLM needs to know. - ❌ **workspace root folder & git repo flag:** In my testing, in a non-git repo directory, workspace root folder is /, and git repo flag is false. While the session remains in the foreground and I run git init in that directory, neither field changes. However, once I exit opencode and resume the session after `git init` or `rm -r .git`, workspace root folder becomes the same as the working directory, and git repo flag becomes true, causing all subsequent token caches to miss. - ❌ **today's date:** After crossing midnight, this field changes, causing all subsequent token caches to miss. DeepSeek servers may keep caches on disk for several hours or even days; the cache miss caused by the date change is unnecessary. Therefore, I suggest the following regarding the env section of the system prompt: - Remove workspace root folder and git repo flag. The agent can use git commands to check whether the current path is a git repo. I don't think this information needs to be in the system prompt. - Remove today's date. The agent can also query this using commands. I don't think this information needs to be in the system prompt either. In addition to the modifications to the env section of the system prompt, I also suggest placing the skill list before env. Because the skill list is more stable than env (e.g., working directory), this will yield better cache hit rates when using opencode in different working paths. Related code `packages/opencode/src/session/system.ts:42-80` OpenCode version: 1.15.10

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Move git/PR instructions out of bash tool description to save ~1.7K tokens per request
signal.text: ﻿## Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ## Describe the enhancement you want to request I was profiling why a fresh OpenCode session starts at ~40K tokens. I downloaded all 16 tool .txt files from `packages/opencode/src/tool/` and measured them. **bash.txt is 9,288 characters (~2,654 tokens). But 63% of it has nothing to do with running bash commands.** The git commit workflow and PR creation instructions account for 5,874 characters (~1,678 tokens) — those are procedural guides, not bash execution semantics. Here's the thing: tool descriptions are sent with every single API request and are **not cacheable**. System prompt text, on the other hand, **is** cacheable (Anthropic prompt caching, OpenAI cached prefix). So those git/PR instructions are being paid for on every turn, even when the user never asks for a commit or PR. The fix is straightforward: move the `# Committing changes with git` and `# Creating pull requests` sections from `bash.txt` into the system prompt template. The model still sees the same instructions — just through a cacheable channel instead of a non-cacheable one. For reference, here's the full breakdown I measured: - bash.txt: 9,288 chars (~2,654 tokens) — 63% git/PR instructions - task.txt: 3,799 chars (~1,085 tokens) - multiedit.txt: 2,406 chars (~687 tokens) - edit.txt: 1,369 chars (~391 tokens) - apply_patch.txt: 1,092 chars (~312 tokens) - read.txt: 1,158 chars (~331 tokens) - lsp.txt: 1,040 chars (~297 tokens) - websearch.txt: 976 chars (~279 tokens) - batch.txt: 998 chars (~285 tokens) - codesearch.txt: 802 chars (~229 tokens) - webfetch.txt: 750 chars (~214 tokens) - question.txt: 657 chars (~188 tokens) - grep.txt: 689 chars (~197 tokens) - write.txt: 623 chars (~178 tokens) - glob.txt: 545 chars (~156 tokens) - ls.txt: 314 chars (~90 tokens) Total: ~26,500 chars (~7,573 tokens) across all built-in tool descriptions. This is complementary to the MCP lazy loading work in #12520 — that PR addresses dynamic MCP tools, while this addresses the static built-in tool overhead. Related: #11995, #17482, #20922.

signal.title: opencode (default mode) closes entire terminal window on Linux / i3wm
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary Running the `opencode` command in its default mode (which starts both the server and the TUI in the same process) causes the **entire terminal window to close** — not just the opencode process exiting, but the emulator window itself disappearing. Running `opencode serve` and `opencode attach <url>` as two separate processes works perfectly, which strongly suggests the bug is in the combined server+TUI startup path. ## Environment - **opencode version:** 1.14.21 - **OS:** Ubuntu (Linux) - **Window manager:** i3wm - **Shell:** zsh with oh-my-zsh - **Terminal emulators tested (all reproduce the bug):** xterm, Terminator, GNOME Terminal - **Installation path:** `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` - **Installation method:** curl installer (`curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`) — inferred from binary location at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open any terminal emulator (xterm, Terminator, GNOME Terminal — all reproduce). 2. Run `opencode` (default mode, no subcommand). 3. The TUI briefly appears, then the **entire terminal window closes**. ## Expected behavior The TUI should start and remain running until the user exits it. The terminal emulator window itself should never be closed by opencode. ## Actual behavior The terminal emulator window disappears entirely. The shell process and the emulator process both terminate. On the next session, running opencode reproduces the same crash. ## What works (workaround) Splitting the server and TUI into two separate processes works reliably: ```bash # Terminal 1 opencode serve --port 4096 # prints: http://127.0.0.1:4096 # Terminal 2 opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:4096 ``` In this mode, the TUI runs normally and the terminal does not close. This strongly suggests the bug is in the code path that launches server + TUI in a single process. ## Diagnostic work already done I ran an extensive elimination pass. The following were all tested and **ruled out** as causes: | Hypothesis | Test | Result | |---|---|---| | Out-of-memory (OOM killer) | `free -h`, `dmesg \| grep -i oom` | 20 GB RAM free, no OOM records | | Terminal emulator bug (VTE) | Tested in xterm (non-VTE) | Crash reproduces | | GPU/renderer issue | Multiple emulators tested | Crash reproduces in all | | Wrong binary architecture | `file $(which opencode)` + `uname -m` | Correct architecture | | Corrupted SQLite database | Moved `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db*` aside | No change | | Corrupted config/cache | Moved `~/.config/opencode/`, `~/.local/share/opencode/`, `~/.cache/opencode/` aside | No change | | Shell environment (zsh, oh-my-zsh, fnm, nvm) | `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin TERM=xterm /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c '~/.opencode/bin/opencode'` | Crash reproduces | | External plugins | `opencode --pure` | Crash reproduces | | Server alone | `opencode serve` | **Works fine** | | TUI alone attaching to external server | `opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:PORT` | **Works fine** | ## Strace findings Running `strace -f -o /tmp/opencode-strace.log opencode` and grepping for fatal signals showed **no SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, SIGKILL, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP** delivered to the main opencode process. Child processes exit cleanly with `exit_group(0)` (one exited with `exit_group(1)`, a grep subprocess whose command resolution I couldn't reconstruct from the log alone). The process disappears without any visible crash signature. The strace does show child processes resetting job-control signal handlers (`SIGTSTP`, `SIGTTIN`, `SIGTTOU` set to `SIG_DFL`) and redirecting stdin via `dup2(3, 0)` — consistent with opencode spawning shell subprocesses for tool calls during startup. My guess at the mechanism (not confirmed): the process that starts both server and TUI may be reparenting or detaching in a way that causes the controlling-TTY session leader to die, which then propagates up to the emulator. But this is speculation — someone familiar with the opentui integration would be far better placed to diagnose the real cause. ## Additional notes - **"Reinstalling" appeared to fix it temporarily** in earlier sessions. After full diagnosis, this was likely coincidental timing rather than a real fix — the crash reproduces consistently from a clean state. - The attach-based workaround is stable and usable indefinitely, so this is not blocking me personally, but the default `opencode` command being unusable on a common Linux configuration (Ubuntu + i3wm) seems worth fixing. ### Plugins linear (disabled) ### OpenCode version 1.14.21 ### Steps to reproduce I installed in the morning, and at night or in the next day the problem occurs when I open the opencode. The last times I just reinstalled, but this time I was able to build this workaround. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS ### Terminal xterm, Terminator, GNOME Terminal

signal.title: [FEATURE]: MCP tool calls should carry current session context (session_id)
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Feature Request When OpenCode calls an MCP tool, the current session ID should be injected into the request so that MCP servers can associate operations with the OpenCode session that triggered them. ### Use Case I built an MCP server (`mcp-memory`) that stores conversation memories. It accepts an optional `session_id` parameter, but when OpenCode's AI agent calls `save_memory`, it doesn't know the current session ID, so memories are saved without session context. This makes it impossible to group memories by the OpenCode session they originated from. ### Proposed Solution Inject the current OpenCode session ID into MCP tool call requests via the `_meta` field of the `CallToolRequest` (following MCP protocol design). This approach works for both local (stdio) and remote MCP servers, unlike solutions that only cover HTTP transport. The MCP server would then extract the session ID from the request context. ### Why this matters Without session context, memory/stateful MCP servers have no way to correlate data with the conversations that produced them, limiting their usefulness for cross-session persistence. ### Relationship to existing issues This request differs from related issues: - **#15117** proposes exposing session context via environment variables (`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`). While valuable, env vars are set at process start and cannot change mid-session. Our `_meta` field approach follows MCP protocol design and works per-request. - **#28225** proposes a plugin hook (`mcp.call.before`) to inject headers into outbound HTTP MCP calls. This only covers remote MCP over HTTP transport. Our `_meta` field approach covers both local (stdio) and remote MCP servers uniformly.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Export actual server URL as environment variable
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem When OpenCode starts its HTTP server, the actual port used is not easily discoverable by child processes. This creates issues for integrations that need to spawn additional OpenCode instances (e.g., tmux panes, background tasks, CI/CD scripts). ### Current Behavior 1. **Server URL discovery relies on `ctx.serverUrl`**, which returns a fallback when no server is running: ```typescript // From server/server.ts export function url(): URL { return _url ?? new URL("http://localhost:4096") // Always returns fallback } ``` 2. **Port auto-fallback is silent**: ```typescript // From server/server.ts:2883 const server = opts.port === 0 ? (tryServe(4096) ?? tryServe(0)) // Tries 4096, then random port : tryServe(opts.port) ``` - If port 4096 is taken, OpenCode silently uses a random OS-assigned port - Child processes have no way to discover the actual port used 3. **Multi-instance conflicts**: - User runs OpenCode in Project A → binds to port 4096 - User runs OpenCode in Project B → falls back to random port (e.g., 49152) - Child processes from Project B can't discover port 49152 ### Real-World Use Case: Tmux Integration Our plugin ([oh-my-opencode-slim](https://github.com/anomalyco/oh-my-opencode-slim)) spawns tmux panes that run `opencode attach <url> --session <id>` to show sub-agent work in real-time. **Current workaround:** - Require users to configure a fixed port: `{ "server": { "port": 4096 } }` - This breaks when multiple OpenCode instances run simultaneously - Port conflicts cause startup failures **What we need:** - Discover the actual server URL dynamically - Support multiple concurrent OpenCode instances on different ports --- ## Proposed Solution Export the actual server URL as an environment variable when the server starts: ```typescript // After server starts successfully (server.ts:2886) const server = opts.port === 0 ? (tryServe(4096) ?? tryServe(0)) : tryServe(opts.port) if (!server) throw new Error(`Failed to start server on port ${opts.port}`) _url = server.url // NEW: Export for child processes process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_URL = server.url.toString() ``` ### Environment Variables to Export | Variable | Example Value | Description | |----------|--------------|-------------| | `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL` | `http://localhost:4096` | Full URL of running server | | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PORT` | `4096` | Port number (optional, for convenience) | ### Benefits 1. **Child processes can discover server**: ```bash # In tmux pane or background task opencode attach $OPENCODE_SERVER_URL --session abc123 ``` 2. **Multi-instance support**: - Each OpenCode instance exports its own URL - Child processes automatically connect to the correct parent 3. **No breaking changes**: - Existing code continues to work - Environment variable is purely additive 4. **Better than file-based coordination**: - Environment variables inherit automatically (Unix convention) - No cleanup required - No file permission issues --- ## Alternative Considered **File-based approach**: Write server URL to `.opencode/.server-url` - **Pros**: Works across all platforms - **Cons**: Requires cleanup, file watching, permission handling, race conditions **Environment variables are cleaner and more Unix-idiomatic.** --- ## Implementation Notes ### Where to Add This In `packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts` after line 2886: ```typescript export function listen(opts: { port: number; hostname: string; mdns?: boolean; cors?: string[] }) { // ... existing code ... const server = opts.port === 0 ? (tryServe(4096) ?? tryServe(0)) : tryServe(opts.port) if (!server) throw new Error(`Failed to start server on port ${opts.port}`) _url = server.url // Export for child processes process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_URL = server.url.toString() process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_PORT = server.port.toString() // ... rest of existing code ... } ``` ### Cleanup on Server Stop ```typescript server.stop = async (closeActiveConnections?: boolean) => { if (shouldPublishMDNS) MDNS.unpublish() // Clean up environment variables delete process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_URL delete process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_PORT return originalStop(closeActiveConnections) } ``` --- ## Example Usage ### Plugin Code (Tmux Integration) ```typescript // Before (hardcoded or unreliable fallback) const serverUrl = ctx.serverUrl?.toString() ?? "http://localhost:4096" // After (dynamic discovery) const serverUrl = process.env.OPENCODE_SERVER_URL ?? ctx.serverUrl?.toString() ``` ### Shell Scripts ```bash #!/bin/bash # Spawn a background OpenCode task connected to the parent server if [ -n "$OPENCODE_SERVER_URL" ]; then opencode attach "$OPENCODE_SERVER_URL" --session "$SESSION_ID" else echo "No OpenCode server found" exit 1 fi ``` --- ## Related - Similar pattern used by tools like `DOCKER_HOST`, `DISPLAY`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` - Follows Unix convention of using environment variables for service discovery - Enables better ecosystem integrations (plugins, scripts, CI/CD) --- Would you be open to this enhancement? Happy to submit a PR if this approach makes sense!

signal.title: [Desktop] Theme dropdown won't reopen immediately after selecting a theme
signal.text: ### Description In the desktop app (Electron), the **Theme** dropdown in *File → Settings → Appearance* (the selector below the Dark/Light mode toggle) stops opening immediately after a theme is selected. It only opens again after clicking somewhere outside the selector first. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the app → hamburger menu → File → Settings 2. In the Appearance section, open the Theme dropdown and select any theme (this works fine) 3. Immediately click the dropdown again to choose another theme ### Expected Behavior The dropdown reopens so another theme can be selected. ### Actual Behavior The dropdown does not open when clicked again immediately after selecting a theme. Behavior differs depending on the state: **Before the second open attempt** (right after selecting a theme): clicking anywhere outside the selector first (anywhere in the settings body, or even right-clicking on the chat canvas) keeps it working - the next click on the dropdown opens it normally. **Once the dropdown has failed to open (stuck state):** - Left-clicking outside the selector no longer helps. At this point, only closing and reopening the Settings panel restores it. - Right-clicking **directly on the selector** does unlock it: a "Select all" text-selection affordance flashes for about a second (as if the control were being treated as plain HTML content), after which left-click opens the dropdown normally. - The **AMOLED** theme is exempt: after selecting it, the dropdown reopens normally without needing any of the above. ### Workaround - To prevent it: click once outside the selector between theme selections. - If already stuck: right-click directly on the selector (ignore the brief "Select all" flash), then left-click to open - or close and reopen Settings entirely. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03b5d2c5-421a-4d83-b237-406e0604593d ### Additional Context Speculation: after applying a theme, some focus/state in the settings UI seems to swallow the next dropdown toggle. AMOLED may be exempt because it is handled differently from the other themes (built-in/native vs. the rest). ### Environment - App: OpenCode Desktop 1.18.19 - OS: Windows 11 IoT Enterprise, Build 26200 (64-bit)

However when I want to copy from OpenCode and then paste back into OpenCode, because I'm trying to repeat back a small bit of text ... signal.title: config: published schema at opencode.ai/config.json rejects documented V2 fields (skills, mcp.*, permissions)
signal.text: ## Summary The JSON Schema served at `https://opencode.ai/config.json` — the URL referenced by `$schema` in every V2 config — describes an older/hybrid shape that does not match current V2 documentation. As a result, editor IntelliSense and any standards-based validator flag **valid V2 configs as invalid**, including configs whose fields are copied verbatim from the V2 docs. This also actively misleads users: for MCP, the stale schema suggests adding an `enabled` key, while V2 explicitly has no `enabled` field. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-beta-17759 - OS: Darwin 27.0.0 (arm64) - Terminal: Apple_Terminal (xterm-256color) - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: beta - Active plugins: one local plugin (`subagent-session-guard.ts`); unrelated to this issue ## Reproduction 1. Create `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` using examples taken verbatim from the V2 docs: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "permissions": [{ "action": "shell", "resource": "git push *", "effect": "ask" }], "skills": ["./team-skills"], "mcp": { "timeout": { "startup": 45000, "catalog": 30000, "execution": 600000 }, "servers": { "everything": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"] } } } } ``` 2. Run `opencode2 debug config` → exits 0, parses and normalizes everything. `opencode2 mcp list` shows the server connecting. The runtime accepts all fields. 3. Validate the same file against the published schema with any JSON-Schema validator: ```sh curl -sS https://opencode.ai/config.json -o schema.json python3 - <<'EOF' import json, jsonschema schema = json.load(open("schema.json")) config = json.load(open("opencode.json")) for err in jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema).iter_errors(config): print("/".join(map(str, err.absolute_path)), "->", err.message) EOF ``` ## Expected Behavior A config following current V2 documentation should validate cleanly against the schema its own `$schema` field points to. ## Actual Behavior The validator reports errors on documented V2 fields: ```text /skills -> ['~/.config/opencode/skills'] is not of type 'object' /mcp/timeout -> {'startup': 45000, ...} is not valid under any of the given schemas /mcp/servers -> {'everything': {...}} is not valid under any of the given schemas / -> Additional properties are not allowed ('permissions' was unexpected) ``` Specific mismatches between the published schema and the V2 docs: | Field | Published schema expects | V2 docs specify | | --- | --- | --- | | `skills` | object `{ "paths": [], "urls": [] }` | plain array of strings: `"skills": ["./team-skills", ...]` | | `mcp` | flat map of server entries, each with optional `enabled` boolean | `mcp.servers.<name>` entries + `mcp.timeout.{startup,catalog,execution}`; **no `enabled` field exists in V2** (servers connect unless `disabled: true`) | | `permissions` | only singular legacy `permission` object | ordered array of `{ action, resource, effect }` rules | Also flagged on a real-world config: `experimental.subagent_depth` and model-level `reasoning_efforts`. The MCP case is worse than cosmetic: because the schema's only accepted shapes mention `enabled`, anyone "fixing" their config to satisfy validators will add a field that V2 does not support. ## Additional Context - This is pure schema/docs drift — the beta runtime handles all of these fields correctly, so the schema appears to predate the V2 config format. - Since V2 configs ship with this `$schema` URL, editors (VS Code, Zed, etc.) show spurious diagnostics on doc-recommended configs, and third-party tooling built on the schema reports the same false positives. - Reproduced consistently with `jsonschema` `Draft202012Validator` (18 errors on a real-world V2 config that loads cleanly in the CLI). - Suggestion: regenerate the published schema from the current V2 types, and/or serve a versioned schema (e.g. `/v2/config.json`) so older editors keep working while V2 configs get accurate validation.

signal.title: fix(core): resolve Bedrock AWS profile credentials for V2
signal.text: Hi I'm from Amazon One Medical, we use Bedrock for everything and was trying out V2 branch and decided to create a patch - I've been using this exact patch locally for about 1.5 weeks and haven't had any issues. ### Issue for this PR Closes #40663 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? V2 maps Amazon Bedrock models to the native provider before the legacy AI SDK credential hook runs. As a result, configured AWS profiles were detected but their credentials never reached the native SigV4 signer. Some AWS environment values, such as `AWS_REGION`, could also be mistaken for bearer credentials. This change: - Separates credential-bearing environment variables from variables that only indicate AWS is configured. - Resolves configured profiles through the AWS default credential chain before creating the native Bedrock model. - Passes the resulting access key, secret key, and session token to the native SigV4 signer. - Preserves explicit static credentials and Bedrock bearer API keys. - Expands regional Bedrock endpoint templates after provider settings are merged, so configured regions are respected. - Reuses the AWS credential provider for each profile while allowing it to refresh temporary credentials. ### How did you verify your code works? - Ran the focused catalog, model resolver, and Bedrock provider tests: 77 passed. - Ran the repository pre-push typecheck: 33 packages passed. - Regenerated the client types. - Built the Linux x64 CLI successfully with `bun run build --single`. - Ran this build with AWS_PROFILE with credentialHelper scripts for about a week of full coding work. This should bring v2 to feature parity with v1. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A, this change has no UI behavior. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: [BUG] Background subagent final response delivered as thousands of duplicated <acp> message-ref tags instead of report text
signal.text: ## Description A background subagent (`task` tool, `background=true`, general agent) completed its work correctly on disk, but the final response delivered to the parent session was corrupted: instead of the actual report text, the parent received ~11K tokens consisting of the literal string `<acp tokens=N type=text>mNNNNN</acp>` repeated hundreds of times, referencing the **child session's own internal message IDs** (e.g. `m00001`–`m00086`). Zero actual report text was delivered. This looks like the message-reference annotation pass (ACP/bili-style context-management tags rendered as `<acp ...>mNNNNN</acp>` prefixes) recursing on or echoing its own output while serializing the child→parent completion payload. ## Environment - OpenCode harness with ACP context-management (bili) tooling - Platform: Windows 11, PowerShell - Subagent type: general, launched with `background=true` - Session context: long-running session (~10 prior subagent completions, heavy bili_compress usage) ## Steps to reproduce Not reliably reproducible yet. Observed twice-shaped failure modes in one session (~10 background subagent runs): 1. **This bug**: child finishes real work (verified independently on disk), final message arrives as thousands of duplicated `<acp>` tag lines instead of text. 2. Related: another run same day ended `state=completed` with **no text at all and no work performed** — matches #32132. ## Observed behavior - Parent received a completion event with an ~11K-token message containing only repeated `<acp tokens=... type=text>mNNNNN</acp>` fragments - The referenced `mNNNNN` ids belong to the child session, not the parent - No error surfaced anywhere; state was `completed` ## Expected behavior - Final assistant text is delivered verbatim exactly once, with at most one annotation prefix per part - If serialization fails or final text is empty, the completion should fail loudly (or retry) rather than deliver garbage/silence ## Impact Parent agents silently lose subagent reports and must independently verify all work (which is what happened here — the work itself was fine). At ~20% of background completions misbehaving in one session, this materially erodes trust in fire-and-forget delegation. ## Suggested fix Sanitize/validate the child→parent completion payload: render annotations exactly once, strip nested/self-referential tag output, and treat an empty final text as an error state rather than a successful completion.

signal.title: fix(core): steer manual compaction by default
signal.text: ## What A manual `/compact` during an active turn now runs at the next step boundary instead of silently waiting for the whole turn — and any queued prompts — to finish. `Session.compact` supported steer delivery all along, but defaulted to `"queue"`, and no client ever passed `delivery`. This flips the default to `"steer"` so user-initiated compaction means "compact soon", not "compact after all queued work". ## Before / After **Before**: `/compact` during a long tool-heavy turn admits a `delivery:"queue"` compaction row. Queue rows are invisible at step boundaries (`runPendingCompaction(sessionID, "steer")` only sees the steer lane), so nothing happens until the turn goes idle — and if a queued prompt was enqueued earlier, the compaction waits behind that entire turn too. The user sees no `Compaction.Started` for the rest of the run and no indication of when it will fire. **After**: `/compact` admits a steer-delivery row. At the next step boundary the runner consumes it ahead of queued prompts, requests the summary, and continues the turn (if steps remain) inside the compacted context. Explicit `delivery: "queue"` keeps the old parking behavior. ## How - `packages/core/src/session.ts`: `Session.compact` default delivery `"queue"` → `"steer"`. - `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`: `runSteps` restructured so every step boundary has one shape — control items first, then a single exit decision, then the model call. The turn continues only while the first step, a continuation, or steer input is owed; deciding after control items means consuming the last steered compaction ends the turn instead of issuing an input-free model call. The drain loop then picks up any queued work. - `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts`: endpoint description updated (no generated client changes; verified `bun run generate` in `packages/client` is a no-op). Ordering semantics are unchanged: enqueue order rules the steer lane, and the compaction row is a barrier. Steers admitted before `/compact` get one more step (so the summary reflects them); steers admitted after it deliver into the fresh compacted epoch. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant I as SessionInbox (steer lane) participant R as SessionRunner participant M as Model R->>M: step N (in flight) U->>I: steer "actually do X" U->>I: /compact (steer, barrier) M-->>R: step N settles R->>I: promote steers up to barrier R->>M: step N+1 (sees "actually do X") M-->>R: step N+1 settles R->>I: consume compaction barrier R->>M: summary request R->>M: continuation in compacted context ``` ## Scope - No TUI/ACP call-site changes needed: they omit `delivery` and inherit the new default. - No change to queued-compaction semantics (`delivery: "queue"` still parks behind earlier queued prompts, per the existing drain-boundary tests). - No hard `compact > steer` priority: a compaction never jumps ahead of steers enqueued before it. That's deliberate — enqueue order stays the single ordering law. ## Testing From `packages/core`: - `bun run test -- test/session-runner.test.ts` — 158 pass, including two new tests: - steer compaction admitted mid-turn runs at the boundary before queued prompts, with an exact request count proving no input-free model call after the barrier - steer compaction admitted mid-tool-turn runs before the turn's continuation step - `bun run test -- test/session-compact.test.ts test/session-prompt.test.ts test/session-execution.test.ts test/session-projector.test.ts test/session-compaction.test.ts` — 80 pass - `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` and `packages/protocol` Existing coverage updated: the default-delivery assertion now expects `steer` (with a new explicit-queue assertion), and the queued-compaction ordering test passes `delivery: "queue"` explicitly.
